About Forest Solutions:

Forest Solutions Inc. (FSI) has been Hawaiʻi’s leading forestry and land management company for over 30 years, specializing in large-scale tree planting, invasive species control, wildfire prevention, native forest restoration, timber plantation management, forest inventory, agroforestry, permitting, and community engagement. We help Hawaii Grow! 

As a team-oriented small business, FSI brings together project managers, foresters, natural resource specialists, technicians, and field crews to address Hawaiʻi’s unique land management challenges. Our work is rooted in scientific best practices, field expertise, and a deep connection to Hawai‘i’s biocultural heritage. FSI has played a key role in shaping large-scale forest management, including supporting active management of over 500,000 acres per year and planting over 1,000,000 native plants across more than 5,000 acres, including the largest native forest restoration project in the state.

This is an opportunity to be part of a diverse and impactful team working on meaningful conservation efforts in Hawaiʻi’s stunning and rugged landscapes.


About the Job:

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Operations Forester to support and lead field-based forest management projects across Hawai‘i Island. This position may be filled at a mid- to senior-level Operations Forester capacity, depending on candidate experience. This position, reporting to our Senior Forester, blends ecological knowledge with hands-on operational leadership and construction oversight in remote and challenging environments. Hawaiʻi’s native forests are among the most ecologically vibrant (and threatened) in the world. If you are driven by the challenge of removing invasive competitors to give native ecosystems room to breathe and thrive, this role offers you the platform, equipment, and scale to make a permanent, positive mark on Hawaiʻi Island’s landscapes.

This position requires someone who thrives in a highly variable environment, with roughly 60% of your time spent outdoors in variable weather and 40% in the office. Field conditions often involve remote off-road driving, cross-country hiking sometimes 10+ miles off trail, navigating thick rain forests as well as dry, hot environments, and conducting quality control checks across projects ranging from small parcels to landscape-scale efforts spanning tens of thousands of acres, with an expectation of 2–3 helicopter flights per year for remote field operations. Office time is reserved for GIS/drone data processing, supply procurement, maintenance logging, taking client & internal meetings, budgeting, proposal creation, and project planning and reporting. Work is project-based and highly responsive to client needs and timelines. Schedule flexibility, a sense of purpose, and self-motivation are essential, in addition to technical skills. 
This role is focused on implementing and managing projects such as wildfire mitigation and fuel reduction, landscape-scale invasive species management, erosion control, large-scale planting operations, access development, and forestry operations. The Operations Forester works closely with the Senior Forester to plan and execute projects, supervise field crews and subcontractors, oversee heavy equipment operations, and ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with ecological objectives.

The ideal candidate is comfortable operating at the intersection of science and agricultural/forestry field operations and able to interpret ecological goals and translate them into practical, on-the-ground implementation strategies. This is an opportunity to work on the frontlines protecting Hawai‘i’s unique biodiversity & ecosystems from aggressive invasive species. This isn't just vegetation management—it's active ecological recovery. You will see the direct results of your labor as treated units transform back into thriving, self-sustaining native Hawaiian habitats. A strong background in ecology, forestry, environmental impacts, or natural resource management, along with excellent organizational and leadership skills, is desirable. 

Flexibility, a sense of purpose, and self-motivation are essential, in addition to technical skills. This is a full-time, year-round position with supervisory responsibilities. Depending on experience, this role may involve supporting project leads or independently managing projects from planning through completion. 

Work locations vary widely and often involve off-road travel throughout Hawaiʻi Island with occasional off-island assignments. This role requires adaptability, strong leadership, sound judgment in remote settings, and the ability to manage evolving project priorities in response to client needs and environmental conditions.

Candidate Selection Criteria:
Candidates will be evaluated for Entry, Mid, or Senior placement based on their background and professional experience in forestry, botany, natural resource management, agriculture, environmental science, conservation biology, ecology, wildlife management, or a related field.

For Entry-Level Placement, candidates must possess a relevant Bachelor’s degree along with a minimum of 2-3 years of relevant field experience. 
For Mid-Level Placement, candidates must possess both a relevant Bachelor’s and Master’s degree combined with 5-8 years of progressive field experience.
For Senior-Level Placement, candidates must possess at least a relevant Master’s degree alongside 10 or more years of extensive industry experience.

An equivalent combination of relevant field experience, specialized training, and education will be considered in lieu of the formal degree requirements for each level. 


Principal Responsibilities:
Assist Senior Operations Forester with project organization, planning, managing field crews & subcontractors, tracking work progress, and inspecting the quality of fieldwork.
Oversee operational safety protocols and OSHA compliance across active field sites, conducting regular hazard assessments, holding safety briefings, and implementing continuous safety improvements.
Collect, process and analyze GPS and GIS data for mapping, reporting, and operational planning.
Supervise heavy equipment operations – site preparation, road maintenance, maintaining equipment maintenance logs.
Ensure the correct use and maintenance of field equipment, tractors, skidder, excavator, crawler tractors, review equipment use logs.
Apply and supervise the application of pesticides in accordance with the label and legal requirements, including personal protective equipment (PPE), verifying correct application methods and safety standards by field crews.
Represent company or clients at public and private meetings in a professional manner.
Assist in preparing annual work budgets, project proposals, and estimating the cost of completing projects.
Plan and track large-scale vegetation management operations using GIS/GPS data, including treatment boundaries, completed acreage, production rates, and field accomplishments for client reporting.
Prepare clear operational reports documenting completed work, acreage, crew and equipment production, field conditions, and project progress.
Help manage large-scale biomass processing and chipping operations, coordinating material handling, equipment, crews, production, and site logistics.
Coordinate preventative maintenance, routine inspections, troubleshooting, and repair scheduling for forestry and biomass-processing equipment, including large chippers (over 18in).
Track equipment productivity, downtime, maintenance needs, and operating costs to help improve project efficiency and future estimating.
Other duties as assigned.


Essential Qualifications:
Willingness and ability to work alone or in small teams in remote locations, with little or no mobile phone coverage.
Working knowledge of field safety practices, hazard recognition, and standard OSHA safety compliance guidelines.
Physically able to walk long distances in rugged terrain, over sharp lava fields or in thick forests for a full workday collecting field data in all weather. Ability to lift 75 lbs.
Experience operating small powered tools safely such as weed eaters, chainsaw, pruners, etc.
Experience in the use of a computer and Microsoft Office suite, basic knowledge of ESRI ArcGIS software, able to upload/download GPS data.
Willing to mix and apply pesticides and chemical fertilizers in strict accordance with label requirements; certified applicator a plus.
Able to drive and tow trailers with 4WD, manual transmission vehicles on rough roads; valid US driver’s license at the time of hire.
Able to legally work in the United States at the time of hire.
Working knowledge of preventative maintenance and basic mechanical troubleshooting for forestry and heavy equipment, including the ability to identify mechanical issues before they result in major equipment failure.
Ability to safely plan and coordinate work around large forestry equipment, including chippers, excavators, dozers, tractors, and material-handling equipment.

Desirable Qualifications:
Knowledge of the ecology of native Hawaiian flora and fauna.
Formal safety certifications a plus (e.g., OSHA 10/30-Hour General Industry/Construction, First Aid/CPR/Wilderness First Responder).
Experience planning or supervising large-scale vegetation management operations, including tracking acres treated, production rates, crew performance, and project costs.
Experience operating, maintaining, or managing industrial forestry or biomass-processing equipment, particularly large whole-tree chippers/grinders.
Strong working knowledge of ArcGIS Pro for operational mapping, treatment tracking, acreage calculations, and preparation of client-ready maps and reports.
Supervisory experience, including as a team leader.
Speak or understand languages other than English; primarily Spanish and ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi.


Compensation & Benefits:
Competitive compensation starts at $60,000 - $80,000+ per year, commensurate with experience; optional vehicle stipend provided for use of personal truck for work & off-road driving, or use of company vehicles; 401K retirement plan; comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, vision) with 100% employer-paid premiums for the employee; and PTO & sick leave policy plus holiday pay.

This position, reporting to our Senior Forester, blends ecological knowledge with hands-on operational leadership and construction oversight in remote and challenging environments. Hawaiʻi’s native forests are among the most ecologically vibrant (and threatened) in the world. If you are driven by the challenge of removing invasive competitors to give native ecosystems room to breathe and thrive, this role offers you the platform, equipment, and scale to make a permanent, positive mark on Hawaiʻi Island’s landscapes.

This position requires someone who thrives in a highly variable environment, with roughly 60% of your time spent outdoors in variable weather and 40% in the office. Field conditions often involve remote off-road driving, cross-country hiking sometimes 10+ miles off trail, navigating thick rain forests as well as dry, hot environments, and conducting quality control checks across projects ranging from small parcels to landscape-scale efforts spanning tens of thousands of acres, with an expectation of 2–3 helicopter flights per year for remote field operations. Office time is reserved for GIS/drone data processing, supply procurement, maintenance logging, taking client & internal meetings, budgeting, proposal creation, and project planning and reporting. Work is project-based and highly responsive to client needs and timelines. Schedule flexibility, a sense of purpose, and self-motivation are essential, in addition to technical skills. 
This role is focused on implementing and managing projects such as wildfire mitigation and fuel reduction, landscape-scale invasive species management, erosion control, large-scale planting operations, access development, and forestry operations. The Operations Forester works closely with the Senior Forester to plan and execute projects, supervise field crews and subcontractors, oversee heavy equipment operations, and ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with ecological objectives.

The ideal candidate is comfortable operating at the intersection of science and agricultural/forestry field operations and able to interpret ecological goals and translate them into practical, on-the-ground implementation strategies. This is an opportunity to work on the frontlines protecting Hawai‘i’s unique biodiversity & ecosystems from aggressive invasive species. This isn't just vegetation management—it's active ecological recovery. You will see the direct results of your labor as treated units transform back into thriving, self-sustaining native Hawaiian habitats. A strong background in ecology, forestry, environmental impacts, or natural resource management, along with excellent organizational and leadership skills, is desirable. 

Flexibility, a sense of purpose, and self-motivation are essential, in addition to technical skills. This is a full-time, year-round position with supervisory responsibilities. Depending on experience, this role may involve supporting project leads or independently managing projects from planning through completion. 

Work locations vary widely and often involve off-road travel throughout Hawaiʻi Island with occasional off-island assignments. This role requires adaptability, strong leadership, sound judgment in remote settings, and the ability to manage evolving project priorities in response to client needs and environmental conditions.

Candidate Selection Criteria:
Candidates will be evaluated for Entry, Mid, or Senior placement based on their background and professional experience in forestry, botany, natural resource management, agriculture, environmental science, conservation biology, ecology, wildlife management, or a related field.

For Entry-Level Placement, candidates must possess a relevant Bachelor’s degree along with a minimum of 2-3 years of relevant field experience. 
For Mid-Level Placement, candidates must possess both a relevant Bachelor’s and Master’s degree combined with 5-8 years of progressive field experience.
For Senior-Level Placement, candidates must possess at least a relevant Master’s degree alongside 10 or more years of extensive industry experience.

An equivalent combination of relevant field experience, specialized training, and education will be considered in lieu of the formal degree requirements for each level. 


Principal Responsibilities:
Assist Senior Operations Forester with project organization, planning, managing field crews & subcontractors, tracking work progress, and inspecting the quality of fieldwork.
Oversee operational safety protocols and OSHA compliance across active field sites, conducting regular hazard assessments, holding safety briefings, and implementing continuous safety improvements.
Collect, process and analyze GPS and GIS data for mapping, reporting, and operational planning.
Supervise heavy equipment operations – site preparation, road maintenance, maintaining equipment maintenance logs.
Ensure the correct use and maintenance of field equipment, tractors, skidder, excavator, crawler tractors, review equipment use logs.
Apply and supervise the application of pesticides in accordance with the label and legal requirements, including personal protective equipment (PPE), verifying correct application methods and safety standards by field crews.
Represent company or clients at public and private meetings in a professional manner.
Assist in preparing annual work budgets, project proposals, and estimating the cost of completing projects.
Plan and track large-scale vegetation management operations using GIS/GPS data, including treatment boundaries, completed acreage, production rates, and field accomplishments for client reporting.
Prepare clear operational reports documenting completed work, acreage, crew and equipment production, field conditions, and project progress.
Help manage large-scale biomass processing and chipping operations, coordinating material handling, equipment, crews, production, and site logistics.
Coordinate preventative maintenance, routine inspections, troubleshooting, and repair scheduling for forestry and biomass-processing equipment, including large chippers (over 18in).
Track equipment productivity, downtime, maintenance needs, and operating costs to help improve project efficiency and future estimating.
Other duties as assigned.


Essential Qualifications:
Willingness and ability to work alone or in small teams in remote locations, with little or no mobile phone coverage.
Working knowledge of field safety practices, hazard recognition, and standard OSHA safety compliance guidelines.
Physically able to walk long distances in rugged terrain, over sharp lava fields or in thick forests for a full workday collecting field data in all weather. Ability to lift 75 lbs.
Experience operating small powered tools safely such as weed eaters, chainsaw, pruners, etc.
Experience in the use of a computer and Microsoft Office suite, basic knowledge of ESRI ArcGIS software, able to upload/download GPS data.
Willing to mix and apply pesticides and chemical fertilizers in strict accordance with label requirements; certified applicator a plus.
Able to drive and tow trailers with 4WD, manual transmission vehicles on rough roads; valid US driver’s license at the time of hire.
Able to legally work in the United States at the time of hire.
Working knowledge of preventative maintenance and basic mechanical troubleshooting for forestry and heavy equipment, including the ability to identify mechanical issues before they result in major equipment failure.
Ability to safely plan and coordinate work around large forestry equipment, including chippers, excavators, dozers, tractors, and material-handling equipment.

Desirable Qualifications:
Knowledge of the ecology of native Hawaiian flora and fauna.
Formal safety certifications a plus (e.g., OSHA 10/30-Hour General Industry/Construction, First Aid/CPR/Wilderness First Responder).
Experience planning or supervising large-scale vegetation management operations, including tracking acres treated, production rates, crew performance, and project costs.
Experience operating, maintaining, or managing industrial forestry or biomass-processing equipment, particularly large whole-tree chippers/grinders.
Strong working knowledge of ArcGIS Pro for operational mapping, treatment tracking, acreage calculations, and preparation of client-ready maps and reports.
Supervisory experience, including as a team leader.
Speak or understand languages other than English; primarily Spanish and ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi.


Compensation & Benefits:
Competitive compensation starts at $60,000 - $80,000+ per year, commensurate with experience; optional vehicle stipend provided for use of personal truck for work & off-road driving, or use of company vehicles; 401K retirement plan; comprehensive healthcare (medical, dental, vision) with 100% employer-paid premiums for the employee; and PTO & sick leave policy plus holiday pay.

Title- Otolith Laboratory Biologist
Classification- Fish & Wildlife Biologist 3
Job Status- Full-Time/Permanent
WDFW Program- Fish Program – Science Division
Duty Station- Olympia, Washington – Thurston County
Posting Timeframe- This recruitment is scheduled to be posted until November 3, 2026. The first review of applications will take place on October 26, 2026. Application review is ongoing, and applicants are encouraged to submit their materials as soon as possible. Following the first review date, this recruitment may be closed at any time.

Learn more about being a member of Team WDFW!


WDFW’s Fish Ageing and Otolith Laboratories provide critical age and origin data to WDFW Fish Management and Hatchery Divisions, tribal co-managers, and federal fisheries managers to be used in forecasting, run reconstruction, stock assessment, and scientific research.

With your expertise in the preparation and processing of calcified structures, you will conduct research and report on biological studies of Pacific Salmon and other marine, anadromous, and freshwater fishes.

Your work as part of the Otolith Laboratory Team will directly support efforts to meet resource and economic needs for the State of Washington and the Pacific Northwest, including programs focused on recovering Endangered Species Act (ESA) sensitive stocks.


What to Expect:
Among the varied range of responsibilities held within this role, the Otolith Laboratory Biologist’s duties will include,

Thermal Mark Implementation and Evaluation:
Prepare high-quality, half-sectioned and thin-sectioned otolith samples.
Use lapping wheels for grinding and polishing.
Communicate effectively with lab team members and supervisor to ensure accuracy and meet project deadlines.
Independently observe otoliths using compound and dissecting microscopes to identify and decode thermal marks.
Accurately records thermal mark information into database.
Review and plan distinctive thermal mark patterns aligned with hatchery requests.
Develop thermal marking schedules.
Coordinate, adapt, and communicate hatchery thermal marking schedules to achieve intended thermal marks.

Microstructural and Microchemical Analyses:
Prepare high-quality samples from otoliths and other calcified structures for microstructural and microchemical analyses using low-speed saws and lapping wheels.
Use image analysis software and microscopes to measure and count daily increments in otoliths to evaluate environmental, ecological, and anthropogenic influences on growth during early life history.
Evaluate and summarize results of daily growth estimates, accuracy and precision of estimates, size-at-marine entry, and other relevant parameters.

Data Collection, Analysis, and Reporting:
Perform statistical analysis and interpretation of data.
Prepare reports, peer-reviewed publications, and presentations at conferences and other meetings.

Assisting and Supporting Production, Thermal Marking Operations, and Field Collections:
Assist hatchery and lab staff with artificially spawning and cross-fertilizing salmonid gametes.
Travel to study sites to assist with or lead collection efforts for biological samples.

 Working Conditions:

Work Setting, including hazards: Work primarily occurs in a laboratory setting, but will also include office environments, hatcheries, and field sites. Perform repetitive fine motor functions for long durations. Extended periods of time will be spent looking at computer monitors or through microscopes.

Laboratory hazards include hot surfaces (hot plates, burners), grinding wheels, sharp blades, dissecting tools, and chemical exposure (acids, ethanol, acetone, thermoplastic resin, and polystyrene resin) both direct and as fumes.

Hatchery and field work may be performed during inclement weather and over slippery, uneven terrain near or on the water. Lift equipment, samples, coolers, and field gear weighing up to 75 pounds, with assistance as needed. Travel will include operating, or being a passenger in, a motor vehicle on highways or dirt roads. This position may involve working in or near water, including tasks that require navigating, negotiating, and performing duties related to water environments.

Schedule: Typically, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. The work schedule may require weekend work or extended hours while in the field.

Travel Requirements: Occasional field work, laboratory work, and projects will require travel throughout Washington state. Attend annual workshops and conferences. Travel may include overnight and day trips. Increased travel potential November–February.

Tools and Equipment: Compound and dissecting (stereo) microscopes, epifluorescence microscope, desktop/laptop computers, image analysis software, dissecting tools, precision grinders, hot plates, fume hood, balances, and low-speed precision saws will be used routinely. Portable chilling units and pumps will occasionally be set up and maintained for hatchery production or controlled experiments.

Customer Interactions: Public interactions are uncommon but may occur when entering state buildings, working at hatcheries, or conducting fieldwork. Collaborate and professionally communicate with Tribal/First Nation groups and co-managers, WDFW staff throughout the state, non-profit organizations, academic groups, public utilities, federal agencies, other Washington state resource agencies, and fisheries agencies from other states.


Qualifications:

Closely related qualifying experience may be substituted for the required education on a year-by-year basis.

Required Qualifications:

Option 1:
A Bachelor's degree in fisheries, biology, natural resource science, environmental science, or a related field.
  AND
Three (3) years of professional experience in fish research or management.

Option 2:
Two (2) years as a Fish & Wildlife Biologist 2.


In addition to meeting one of the options listed above, the following are also required and may be gained concurrently:

One (1) year of experience with the following:
Processing or analyzing calcified structures.
Producing high-quality otolith sections, including preparing and analyzing otoliths for thermal mark interrogations, microstructure, and/or microchemistry analysis.
Reading and interpreting multiple band otolith patterns, including reading/evaluating calcified structures for age estimation or thermal mark patterns.

Ability to:
Accurately perform repetitive motions utilizing fine motor skills for long periods of time.
Prepare 20-40 otolith thin sections and 50-100 otolith half sections daily.
Read 100-300 otolith samples daily.

Knowledge of:
Pacific salmon life history and growth.


Please Note:
A Master’s degree in the applicable science may substitute for one (1) year of the required experience in fish research or management.
A Ph.D. in the applicable science may substitute for two (2) years of the required experience in fish research or management.

 Certifications/Licenses:
Valid Driver’s License.


Preferred Qualifications:
In addition to the required qualifications, our ideal applicant will possess some or all the following:

Master’s degree in a relevant biological science.
Authorship or co-authorship of one (1) or more peer-reviewed publications.

Experience:
Processing and analyzing data obtained from otoliths or other calcified structures.
Applying current fish ageing research methods.
Enumerating daily growth increments in otoliths.
Otolith thermal mark identification.
With, or knowledge of, Pacific Northwest fish biology and ecology, including life history and population dynamics.
Managing multiple complex projects with competing deadlines, producing accurate and timely work.
Analyzing data to evaluate issues, assess options, draw conclusions, and support decision-making.
Defining research questions, identifying data needs, and designing independent experiments.

 Your application must include the following:
A completed online application showcasing how your qualifications align with the job requirements.
An up-to-date resume.
A cover letter detailing your interest in the position, your relevant skills and experience, and why you are the ideal candidate.
At least three professional references with current contact information.

General Statement | As recreational use of public lands increases, managers need scientific guidance to balance recreation access with ecological protection. This project will synthesize and advance the state of recreation ecology science to better inform management decision-making, with a focus on federally designated Wilderness and similarly protected areas. Research themes include:

Developing a contemporary conceptual framework to help managers address challenges associated with recreation ecology within areas of the National Wilderness Preservation System.Characterizing trade-offs between recreational use and ecological conditions at multiple spatial and temporal scales.Evaluating management concerns related to recreation impacts on natural resources (water quality, vegetation, soils, wildlife).Proposing novel adaptive approaches to recreation in wilderness areas.
Duties and Responsibilities | Conduct a comprehensive literature review on the state of science in recreation ecology.Review management plans and guidance documents to evaluate how recreation ecology influences land management decisions.Engage with federal public land managers to understand decision-making processes and information needs.Identify and compile secondary datasets (monitoring records, visitor use data, trail locations) relevant to recreation impacts.Design and conduct novel analyses using existing data to generate insights into relationships between recreation and ecological responses.Lead writing of at least one peer-reviewed manuscript and one manager-oriented report.Archive project data in accordance with federal data management requirements.Present findings to managers, agency partners, and scientific audiences.
Required Qualifications – Experience, Education, Knowledge & Skills | PhD in ecology, conservation biology, environmental science, natural resource management, or a closely related field by start date.Experience with literature synthesis or systematic review methods.Strong quantitative skills and experience with statistical analysis or spatial data.Demonstrated experience or potential for translating scientific research and technical information into written and oral presentations for scientific and practitioner audiences.
Preferred Qualifications – Experience, Education, Knowledge & Skills | Background in recreation ecology, visitor use management, or protected area management.Experience working with or for federal land management agencies (USFS, BLM, NPS, or USFWS).Familiarity with wilderness policy and the National Wilderness Preservation System.Proficiency in R, Python, or GIS platforms.
The Successful Candidate Will | Possess excellent written and oral communication skills, including writing for both scientific and practitioner audiences.Have the ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary research environment.Represent the department, college, and university to others in a professional and courteous manner.

Description
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting candidates to fill the role of a full-time Microbiology Technician 2. This position is benefits-eligible with an anticipated start date of December 15th, 2026.
Northern fur seals are important predators in the Bering Sea ecosystem and consume commercially and ecologically important fish and squid species. Timely information on fur seal diets is needed to understand population trends and inform ecosystem-based fisheries management. Traditionally, diet information has been obtained by identifying prey hard parts recovered from fecal samples, a process that requires extensive staff time and specialized expertise. DNA metabarcoding provides an efficient approach for identifying prey species and can improve taxonomic resolution. It also provides opportunities to characterize the diets of individually monitored animals and relate diet to foraging behavior, health, and reproductive success. We are seeking a laboratory technician to support a collaborative project involving the Alaska Fisheries Science Center’s Auke Bay Laboratories Genetics Program, Marine Mammal Laboratory, and Alaska Department of Fish and Game to advance DNA-based methods for studying northern fur seal diets.
The technician will generate DNA metabarcoding data from northern fur seal scat and fecal loop samples collected on St. Paul, St. George, and Bogoslof Islands. The work will entail DNA extraction, PCR amplification and optimization, preparation of sequencing libraries, and quality control of resulting data. The technician will also assist with testing cephalopod-specific metabarcoding primers and generating reference sequences from identified prey specimens to improve detection and identification of squid and other cephalopods. These efforts will support comparisons among scat subsamples, between scat and fecal loop samples, and between DNA metabarcoding and traditional hard parts analysis. Deliverables will include sequencing files, associated sample metadata, quality-controlled prey identification data, and reports summarizing laboratory methods and data quality. These products will contribute to developing timely estimates of fur seal diet composition and prey consumption for use in fisheries and ecosystem assessments.
Essential Functions 
Conduct genetics laboratory work, including processing northern fur seal scat and fecal loop samples, extracting DNA, and performing PCR.
Following established protocols, prepare DNA metabarcoding libraries for high-throughput sequencing, including amplicon and indexing PCR, library cleanup, quantification, and pooling.
Assist with testing and optimizing fish- and cephalopod-specific metabarcoding primers and generating reference sequences from identified prey specimens.
Apply contamination prevention procedures and use appropriate controls and technical replicates to assess the quality and consistency of laboratory results.
Maintain organized sample inventories, laboratory records, and sample metadata linking sequencing results to collection information.
Use established bioinformatics workflows and statistical tools to assist with sequence quality control, prey identification, and comparisons among sample types and analytical methods.
Identify and recommend minor modifications to laboratory techniques, document methods and results, and prepare summaries for project investigators.
Knowledge Required by the Position The employee must have knowledge of:

Laboratory methods in molecular biology/genetics laboratories
PCR: primer development, PCR optimization, analyzing results
natural sciences
Knowledge of molecular biology.
Knowledge of aquatic sciences.
Knowledge of Windows-based computer applications such as word processing, spreadsheets, presentation software, database software, molecular biology software.
Supervisory Controls Work is assigned on a daily or weekly basis in terms of project objectives, individual objective, and basic priorities. The employee plans and carries out the assignment with independence, following established protocol. The incumbent seeks assistance only as needed. When common technical and procedural problems arise, the employee exercises initiative in developing solutions. Accuracy of the data produced, quality of the observations made, and sufficiency of planning and execution are normally accepted without detailed review.

Reviews are utilized to ensure that the employee works effectively and produces high quality end products.

Guidelines Guides may be laboratory protocols, analytical protocols, sampling methodologies, standing operating procedures, oral instructions, equipment or instrument manuals, and/or hardware/software manuals.

The guides often require careful study or cross-referencing to locate the applicable rule or answer and can involve some interpretation or judgment to resolve the issue.

Complexity The employee is expected to select and execute the proper approach to completing the work. The assigned duties often have steps or processes which vary, depending on factors such as the reason the work is being performed or the conditions under which it is being performed. The employee is expected to exercise independence in recognizing such differences, in choosing the right course of action, and then in selecting and executing the proper approach to completing the work.

Scope and Effect Work products directly affect the design and execution of experiments and the adequacy of long range investigations, tests, or research conclusions.

Personal Contacts Contacts are with employees in PSMFC; federal, state, or tribal agencies; university researchers, private/non-profit organizations, and the general public.

Purpose of Contacts The purpose of contacts is to exchange information and ensure that project goals are being met through coordination and planning. Communication between contacts affords resolution of problematic issues and serves as an information network.

Physical Demands The work is largely sedentary. There is some walking and bending and lifting of materials and supplies.

Work Environment The work is performed in a laboratory environment, with adequate heating, lighting, and ventilation.

At the lower end of the range, candidates must present one year of Specialized Experience** OR a semester of graduate education that is directly related to the work of the position. Description
 Oregon State University (OSU) and the US Forest Service (USFS) are seeking applicants for a one-year postdoctoral scholar position with the Conservation Biology Program at the Institute for Natural Resources at Oregon State University and the Rocky Mountain Research Station with the USFS. Funding is available for an extension of two additional years contingent upon performance. The selected researcher will work with Dr. Tavis Forrester (USFS) and Dr. Sean Matthews (OSU) to conduct grizzly bear research in collaboration with the Interagency Grizzly Bear Committee Science Team. The researcher will use human mobility data in collaboration with Dr. Mark Ditmer of the Rocky Mountain Research Station to evaluate illegal motorized use on closed roads on public land and grizzly bear movement and habitat use in relation to illegal motorized use. The researcher will also work on a review paper that summarizes the literature relating to secure habitat for grizzly bears. Research resulting from this position will inform habitat management for grizzly bears on USFS land throughout grizzly bear range in the contiguous US. The desired starting date for the position is the winter of 2026/2027. Salary for the position starts at $70,000 per year with salary increases each year. The postdoc will work at the Rocky Mountain Research Station lab located on the campus of the University of Montana. 

Send a cover letter and CV to Tavis Forrester at [email removed] to apply.

A PhD degree in wildlife biology, ecology, statistics, or similar fields 
A record of publishing in peer-reviewed scientific journals. 
Proficiency with data analysis and the use of code for data analysis (R, Python, BUGS/JAGS, Stan, etc.) 
Ability to communicate and collaborate with research groups 
Desire to produce science that is relevant to conservation 
Desire and ability to build a positive, team oriented, and safe working environment for all backgrounds and identities.

Cal Poly Humboldt is searching for a graduate student (MSc) for a partially funded research project conducting at-sea population monitoring of threatened Marbled Murrelet (Brachyramphus marmoratus) and other seabirds in California and Oregon. This work is part of a long-term monitoring project mandated by the Northwest Forest Plan, and is in collaboration with Oregon State University. 

Organization: Department of Wildlife, Cal Poly Humboldt

Position description: The position will begin in May 2027. The successful candidate will participate in at-sea surveys for Marbled Murrelet and all other marine birds in near coastal areas throughout northern California and southern Oregon during the breeding season (~May 15 - July 31). The candidate will be mentored by Drs. Daniel Barton and Frank Fogarty (Cal Poly Humboldt), and Dr. Rachael Orben (Oregon State University). There is the opportunity to investigate research questions related to population trends for other species in a long-term data set. The successful candidate is also expected to participate in at-sea surveys throughout the Oregon coast in 2027, contingent on funding. The position includes field travel and housing, tuition, full-time summer salary and part-time academic year salary (~$20/hr), with the possibility of additional salary support from teaching assistant positions. 

Required qualifications:

·         BSc in biology, zoology, wildlife ecology, fisheries, or a related field

·         Strong oral and written communication skills

·         Ability to work both independently and as part of a team to achieve research goals

·         Willingness to travel and collect data in challenging conditions on small boats

·         Bird identification experience (especially PNW seabirds)

·         Interest in developing advanced quantitative skills 

·         The selected candidate will need to successfully apply to Cal Poly Humboldt’s Master of Science in Natural Resources program.

Preferred qualifications:

·         Experience using GIS and R to manage and analyze wildlife data
·         Experience collecting field data, including conducting point counts or other distance sampling methods
·         Familiarity with working on small boats in ocean conditions.

Coastal Systems Program (CSP) | School for Marine Science and Technology (SMAST)
Location: New Bedford, Massachusetts
Position: Full-time | Job #530332

Position Description

The Coastal Systems Program (CSP) at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth is seeking a Technical Associate (Research Technician) to support coastal, estuarine, freshwater, and watershed research and monitoring.

The position involves intensive field sampling, laboratory analyses, scientific instrumentation, environmental data management, and quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC). The successful candidate will work with faculty, researchers, and students to investigate and monitor the ecological health of coastal Massachusetts.

Primary Responsibilities

Conduct field sampling from shorelines, docks, boats, and marshes.

Collect, preserve, transport, and process environmental samples following established SOPs, QAPPs, and chain-of-custody procedures.

Operate, calibrate, maintain, and troubleshoot water-quality instruments and laboratory equipment.

Assist with laboratory analyses, sample preparation, reagent preparation, and laboratory operations.

Analyze and quality-check environmental data and maintain accurate field logs, laboratory records, and electronic databases.

Assist with field planning, sampling logistics, equipment preparation, and inventory management.

Train and supervise student researchers and temporary research staff.

Assist with scientific reports, presentations, publications, and grant proposals.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in marine science, environmental science, biology, chemistry, oceanography, natural resources, or a related field.

Hands-on field, laboratory, or technical research experience related to environmental, marine, aquatic, or water-quality research.

Ability and willingness to travel to field sites and work irregular hours, including early mornings, evenings, and weekends.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in a closely related field.

Experience with coastal or estuarine water-quality monitoring, environmental sampling, and laboratory analysis.

Small-boat operations and marine fieldwork experience.

SCUBA certification; scientific diving experience is desirable.

Experience with environmental sensors or aquatic monitoring technologies.

Familiarity with SOPs, QA/QC, environmental data management, Excel, MATLAB, R, or GIS.

How to Apply

Applicants must submit a letter of interest, current resume, and contact information for three professional references through the official UMass Dartmouth application portal.

Apply online:
https://careers.umassd.edu/en-us/job/530332/technical-associate-estuarine-and-ocean-sciences

Applications will be reviewed until the position is filled.

Applicants must be authorized for permanent employment in the United States. Employment-based visa sponsorship is not available.

Description
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting candidates to fill the role of a Fishery Biologist 2 at the USGS Western Fisheries Research Center (WFRC) in Seattle, WA. This position is full‑time, benefits-eligible with a one‑year contract that is likely to be extended annually. The anticipated start date is November 16th, 2026.
 
The role supports research on the ecology and life history of salmonids and other Pacific Northwest species from freshwater and marine environments, spanning multiple trophic levels. The position is embedded within the Ecology Life History Lab focusing on Age, Growth, and Food Web Dynamics. They routinely process and analyze otoliths, scales, fin rays, diet samples, zooplankton, drift samples, and other biological materials relevant to threatened fish, their predators, competitors, and prey.

Primary duties include processing biological samples, assessing life‑history characteristics, and supporting food‑web and bioenergetics research. A key responsibility of this position is conducting diet analysis of various predators (both fish and avian), including identification of prey species such as freshwater and marine fishes and invertebrates, and quantifying diet composition to support trophic‑dynamics research. Analysis of otoliths and scales requires processing, measuring and interpreting life‑history characteristics from digital microscopic images. Diet analysis requires accurate taxonomic identification of prey items across diverse habitats. Additional laboratory duties include preparing samples for stable isotope analysis and conducting bomb calorimetry for bioenergetics modeling. General tasks include sample and data collection, sample processing, wet‑lab experiments, care of live fish, maintenance of lab equipment, data entry, data analysis, and contributions to reports and publications.

Applicants should be detail‑oriented, organized, self‑motivated, and able to work independently with minimal supervision. Prior experience with the sample processing and analytical techniques described above and with digital imaging software is preferred. Applicants should be proficient with word‑processing and spreadsheet software.
 
Essential Functions:  Included in this band are professional positions that perform recurring assignments ranging from moderate difficulty where conventional or straight-forward biological concerns are encountered to complex assignments where specialized knowledge and demonstrated competence in advanced techniques are required.  (The functions listed below are characteristic of the type and level of work associated with this group and pay band.  They are not all-inclusive. Individual positions may perform some or all, as well as other similar work.) 
At the lower end of the range, Fishery Biologists have a solid working knowledge of established scientific methods and techniques to perform recurring assignments of moderate difficulty.  Methods and techniques are well established, apply to most situations, and do not require significant deviations.  Resource planning reports generated by employees at this level involve conventional biological concerns.  Reports generated may be short-range management plans or portions of annual work plans.  Lower range work examples include:
Following existing protocols for fish health screenings; conduct tissue sample collection, bacterial testing and analyses, blood collection and analyses, parasite identification, and necropsies on experimental fish populations. Recommend modifications of existing research protocols. Design data collection forms and set up research databases for integration of data. Compile and analyze data for reports, prepare graphics, contribute to or write papers for peer-reviewed journals, and present research results at professional meetings.
Develop age composition structures, stock assessments, escapement totals, harvest levels, run reconstruction frameworks, and/or run forecasts for designated fish species and stock. Evaluate and direct sampling efforts or reporting practices to best meet data requirements. Write memoranda and reports necessary for transfer of information to the appropriate individuals, agencies, and organizations.
Plan, schedule, and conduct behavioral, physiological, morphological, and survival evaluations of hatchery and/or experimental fish populations. Oversee and assist with fish culture tasks for study purposes and recommend procedure variations. Write or contribute to papers and reports for publication, and compile reports on results of data collection and analysis. Prepare and deliver formal and informal presentations at seminars, meetings, etc.
Plan, design, schedule, and conduct fish catch and effort surveys for marine fisheries. Utilize existing general creel survey protocols and determine modifications that address specific marine fisheries conditions or special fisheries. Work with state, federal and regional fishery management councils to provide data on fisheries catch and effort and population trends as well as biology of marine fish species. Work with stock assessment biologists in relation to fisheries-specific data utilized in their stock assessments. Assist with database presentations of the data collected. Prepare reports and presentations as requested. Provide expertise in improvements to the design of creel surveys
Conduct limited physical and biological watershed, stream, and fish habitat assessments. Responsible for conducting data investigation and research, drafting technical report, database management, GIS for all physical and biological data, and survey and inventory results. Prepare, present, implement and update watershed assessment plans.
Assist in writing contract proposals and progress reports. Assist in developing detailed contract specifications, task statements, quality of work criteria, and other specifications.
Monitor budget expenses for projects, control purchasing, and manage equipment inventories.
At the upper end of the range, the Fishery Biologist has specialized knowledge and demonstrated competence in advanced techniques of a complex area of fish biology sufficient to serve as a troubleshooter or specialist.  The employee is competent to modify or adapt standard techniques, processes and procedures, and to assess, select, apply precedents and devise strategies and plans to overcome significant problems related to species production, protection, habitat restoration, or program management and evaluation. Planning reports generated by employees at this level assess the impact of various multi-faceted management or public practices on a resource. Upper range work examples include:

Use biological information to evaluate run profiles and habitat suitability in stocked streams within a major geographical area. Develop comprehensive management plans to insure preservation, protection, and enhancement of habitats.
Plan, design and implement research studies on fish health and/or nutrition. Analyze and report biological and/or genetic information affecting future selection, rearing, and spawning activities.
Prepare both quarterly progress and annual reports on run status and hatchery or fish facility operations.
Monitor and evaluate hatching, rearing and planting of fish. Evaluate and monitor adult return rates. Develop new rearing strategies.
Prepare fish habitat measurement plans or management plans for a watershed or large geographic area.
Diagnose various fish diseases or nutritional disorders in experimental populations or brood stock. Develop modifications to existing health protocols as well as experimental protocols.
Write publishable reports of research and project findings. 
Knowledge Required by the Position: 

Knowledge of fishery biology (including knowledge of particular species of fish) .
Knowledge of microbiology.
Knowledge of fish husbandry.
Knowledge of aquatic habitats.
Knowledge of the scientific method.
Knowledge of sampling protocols.
Knowledge of Windows-based computer applications such as:
word processing
spreadsheets
e-mail
publishing software
presentation software
database software
topographic software
bibliographic software
statistical analysis packages.
Knowledge of technical writing protocols.
Knowledge of advanced statistical analysis and mathematics.
Additional Mandatory Skills:  

valid driver's license
fish species ID skills               
specific software (spreadsheet, word processing, database management, GIS, statistical analysis, behavioral analysis, bibliographic)
oral communication skills                              
written communication skills              
Physical Demands:
Demands generally range from sedentary to moderate --where there is walking, climbing stairs and ladders, reaching, lifting, bending, or extended periods of standing. Some Fishery Biologists in this range have rigorous physical demands where they must be able to handle buckets of water or gear weighing from 40 - 50 pounds, engage in long daily periods of hiking, camp out for extended periods, or maintain footing in fast-moving water.


Work Environment:
Some work is performed in an office setting with adequate lighting, heating and ventilation. Some work may be performed in a laboratory setting which exposes the biologist to odors, chemicals, fish blood, and molds. The employee must use safety precautions including MSDS, gloves, hood, and eye protection. Some employees may work on narrow, elevated walkways and platforms that are over or adjacent to water. Field work involves exposure to all types of weather, slippery rocks or docks, trails, irregular terrain, insects, poison oak, rough or fast-moving water, or cold water temperatures. Work at high elevations or aboard boats may be required.


Qualifications
Minimum Qualification Requirements:
A range of education and experience may be presented.  At the lower end of the range, candidates must present successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major in biological science with at least 6 semester hours in aquatic subjects and at least 12 semester hours in the animal sciences.  In addition to the undergraduate degree requirement, candidates for positions at the lower end of the range must also present 1 year of Specialized Experience** OR 2 years of progressively higher graduate education leading to a master's degree in fields directly related to the position being filled. An equivalent combination of experience and education is also qualifying.
At the upper end of the range, in addition to the undergraduate course of study described above, candidates must also must present one year of Specialized Experience**  OR  3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph. D. degree or equivalent doctoral degree in fields directly related to the position being filled.  An equivalent combination of experience and education is also qualifying.
**Specialized Experience is experience that equips the applicant with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position being filled.  To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower level in the normal line of progression for the position being filled.

Western Fisheries Research Center

12 months or more

0% - 25%

Benefits
Full-Year Employees working at least 30 hours a week are covered by the Company's Life, LTD and AD&D plan. They are eligible to enroll in medical, dental and vision insurance, as well as short term disability, voluntary Life, LTD and AD&D insurance, flexible spending and deferred compensation. An employee receives up to 120 hours of vacation during their first three years of service. After that, the amount of vacation increases every three years of service up to a maximum of 192 hours per year.

Driving
State Vehicle - Valid driver's license required. Offers of employment contingent upon passing driving records check.

$69,373-$109,122/annually

The Freshwater Community Ecology Lab at The Ohio State University (OSU) is seeking a postdoctoral researcher to investigate how fish movement influences the effectiveness of mechanical control strategies for invasive species. This position will focus on building simulation models for smallmouth bass in the Upper Colorado River working with collaborators from the US Geological Survey and the Upper Colorado River Endangered Fish Recovery Program. The researcher will evaluate how varying hypotheses regarding fish movement interact with mechanical removal scenarios to best control smallmouth bass populations.

This researcher will also have opportunities to get involved with and potentially lead other projects in the Freshwater Community Ecology Lab, including projects focused on stream fish community dynamics, movement, estimating demographic rates, and identifying drivers of population dynamics in a wide range of systems including wadable streams in Ohio, the Colorado River, and Lake Erie.

Key Responsibilities
• Develop quantitative demographic models to test population sensitivity under diverse removal and movement scenarios.
• Translate model outputs into actionable management insight for agency partners.
• Work as part of a collaborative research team
• Lead manuscript drafting for peer-reviewed journals, prepare reports, and present findings at regional and national conferences

Qualifications
Required:
• Ph.D. in Ecology, Fisheries Science, Quantitative Biology, or a closely related field
• Strong publication and presentation record relative to career stage
• Excellent communication skills and comfort working with collaborative groups
Preferred:
• Strong background in quantitative ecology, population modeling, and simulation tools
• Prior experience working collaboratively on research projects

About the Environment
The successful applicant will join the Freshwater Community Ecology Lab under supervision of Dr. Lindsey Bruckerhoff (https://u.osu.edu/bruckerhofflab/ ). The Freshwater Community Ecology Lab is part of OSU’s Aquatic Ecology Laboratory (AEL), a collaborative and dynamic research facility within the Department of Evolution, Ecology, and Organismal Biology. The AEL brings together faculty, postdocs, graduate students, and technicians focused on management-driven freshwater research. Learn more about our lab community and research facilities at ael.osu.edu.

How to Apply
To inquire, please submit a Curriculum Vitae (CV) including contact information for three professional references via email to [email removed].

Description
About RCF:

Founded on the principle that conservation is everyone’s responsibility, The Ricketts Conservation Foundation works with private and public partners to study, protect, and enhance the populations of at-risk species within the Yellowstone Ecosystem, while working to understand how our lands can be sustainably managed.

Job Summary:

The Avian Program Lead will oversee and assist with multiple Ricketts Conservation Foundation (RCF) projects in and around the Yellowstone Ecosystem (YE), administer permits and annual reports to federal and state agencies, work with the Director and other RCF employees to implement conservation projects, analyze data, publish results in appropriate peer-reviewed and popular outlets, represent RCF at professional and public events, and initiate new projects in consultation with the director.

Responsibilities:

·        Lead RCF’s Yellowstone Ecosystem Common Loon and Trumpeter Swan projects.
·        Oversee other avian projects in coordination with associate biologist and work with graduate students to complete their research.
·        Work with the director and project heads to recruit, interview, hire, and train seasonal staff. 
·        Assist as needed with project fieldwork (e.g. bird banding, bird surveys).
·        Coordinate with appropriate resource agencies (obtain permits and write annual reports).
·        Disseminate research results via final reports, peer-reviewed print scientific journals, online scientific journals, books, book chapters or other outlets. 
·        Present on findings to scientific and conservation organizations.
·        Initiate new conservation projects in consultation with the director.
·        Provide constructive and timely performance evaluations. 
·        Perform other related duties as assigned. 

Required Skills/Abilities: 

·        Demonstrated ability to conduct scientific research and publish results.
·        Demonstrated ability to perform field work (e.g. avian surveys, bird banding).
·        Excellent verbal and written communication skills. 
·        Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
·        Excellent time management skills with a proven ability to meet deadlines.
·        Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
·        Strong supervisory and leadership skills.
·        Able to assist project leaders achieve their goals. 
·        Ability to prioritize tasks and to delegate them when appropriate.
·        Proficient with ARC-GIS, Excel, and database management.
·        Data visualization and graphic design skills desirable
·        Backcountry skills and experience
·        Commitment to wildlife conservation.

Desired Skills/Abilities

·        Familiarity with the Yellowstone Ecosystem and its flora and fauna.
·        Ability with chainsaws, ATVs, snowmobiles, manual transmission trucks, and motorized watercraft.
·        Comfortable living in a rural environment (~35 miles from Jackson Hole, WY, 40 miles from Pinedale, WY).

Education and Experience:

A master’s degree in a field related to conservation, wildlife biology, or similar field required. Experience managing field research projects, supervising field technicians, conducting original research, and publishing such research is required.

Physical Requirements: 

Position includes working with employees in the field, primarily within the YE. Ability to hike and camp in rugged back country terrain, lift and carry a 50 lb. pack, and use power tools (e.g., chain saw) required.

Pay, Benefits and Work Responsibilities

Pay: $70,000/year

Housing allowance: $15,000/year. 

Remote Work: Allowable December 1 – February 15.

Professional Dues: RCF pays all professional dues for organizations related to conservation mission (e.g. AOS, TWS), as approved by Director.

Conferences: RCF pays registration fees and travel costs to three (3) conferences/year, as approved by Director.

Full benefits include medical insurance, paid vacation, and 401(k).

Work Duties

Project administration: 20%, Permit and Report writing: 10%. Field Work: 25%, Strategic Planning: 10%, Public Outreach: 10%, Develop Standard Operation Procedures and maintain long-term archives 10%, initiate and manage new projects 10%, Coordinate with social media team 5%. Responsibilities will change over time in coordination with the RCF Director.

Application Process

Please email a PDF to [email removed] containing the following information: (1) cover letter stating your interest and qualifications (2) an up-to-date CV (3) contact information for three professional references.

Walter Wehtje
3077570527

Description
Title: Manager, Geospatial Scientist
Department/Division Name: Keller Science Action Center
Supervisor of Position: Nigel Pitman, Sr Conservation Ecologist
Grade: 10
Apply here.

Position Summary:

The Field Museum's Keller Science Action Center (KSAC) translates museum science, collections, and partnerships into results for conservation and quality of life. Our interdisciplinary teams of ecologists, social scientists, and specialists work with communities, scientists, conservation practitioners, and public agencies to co-create knowledge and action for biodiversity conservation, territorial management and human well-being. The Manager, Geospatial Scientist oversees and develops the application of geospatial science across KSAC's Andes-Amazon and Chicago Region programs.

Manager, Geospatial Scientist provides the advanced technical skills and strategic thinking to make KSAC a leader in the management and application of spatial data for conservation. The position combines advanced technical expertise with management, ensuring that spatial analysis, remote sensing, cartography, and data systems directly inform KSAC projects, from the initial planning stages through execution, data analysis, and follow-up. The Manager, Geospatial Scientist will proactively identify high-impact opportunities for KSAC, translate complex spatial information into actionable insights for our staff and partners, and guide multiple initiatives from scoping through delivery and evaluation. Expected projects include expert participation in biological and social inventories of remote areas of the Andes-Amazon region; modeling of biotic and abiotic assets of unvisited natural areas; application of novel remote-sensing technologies to inventory large tropical landscapes; and monitoring of conservation impacts and interventions.

This position works closely with ecological and social scientists, community engagement specialists, program leaders, museum colleagues, and spatial data science leaders in partner organizations. The Manager, Geospatial Scientist establishes shared geospatial standards, oversees quality and spatial data governance, manages staff and collaborators, and strengthens geospatial capacity across teams and partner organizations. The role is expected to balance technical leadership with responsive, relationship-based collaboration.


Duties and Responsibilities:

Provide leadership in design and implementation of geospatial science in support of KSAC’s conservation, territorial management and strategic planning. Work with Andes-Amazon and Chicago Region program teams to identify priority spatial questions, develop analytical approaches that advance program strategies and partner-defined conservation goals, and lead multiple initiatives providing effective project management and implementation, work plans, indicators, publications.
Supervise staff to support geospatial management and analysis. Develop staff leadership capacities and effective collaboration with partners in academia, communities, Indigenous federations, government agencies and conservation organizations. 
Identify strategic opportunities to expand geospatial programming and funding, and collaborate on grant writing, budget management, progress evaluation, reporting and communications that strengthen Action Center programs and projects in Andes-Amazon and Chicago.
Integrate satellite and aerial imagery, field observations, biodiversity inventories, climate and environmental data, participatory mapping, and appropriate social and cultural information into interdisciplinary assessments and analyses including land-use and land-cover change, habitat and ecological connectivity, climate vulnerability and resilience, hydrology, and socio-environmental dynamics.

Evaluate and selectively apply emerging methods such as machine learning, GeoAI, cloud-based remote sensing, automated change detection, and predictive modeling; ensure that methods are scientifically appropriate, explainable, and validated.

Professional development, museum citizenship.

Required Qualifications:

Advanced degree in geography, GIS/geospatial science, ecology, environmental science, remote sensing, earth system science, conservation science, anthropology, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

Minimum seven years of progressively responsible experience in GIS, remote sensing, spatial analysis, applied conservation science, or a closely related field, including technical leadership.

Demonstrated ability to manage projects, including scopes, work plans, schedules, budgets, deliverables, partner relationships, and quality review.

Advanced proficiency with Esri platforms, QGIS, geospatial analysis workflow, programming and analytical environments (e.g., R, Python, Google Earth Engine).

Demonstrated experience with satellite imagery, raster analysis, spatial statistics or modeling, cartography, spatial databases, and integration of large or multi-source environmental datasets.

Effective spatial data management, including metadata, quality assurance and quality control, data security and sharing, and long-term stewardship.

Ability to convert complex analyses into clear findings, visualizations, recommendations, and decision-support products for scientific, community, policy, donor, and public audiences.

Experience supervising or mentoring staff and coordinating multidisciplinary, multicultural, or multi-institutional teams.

Fluency in Spanish or Portuguese, with strong professional proficiency in the other language preferred. 

Working knowledge and/or direct experience with conservation, territorial management, or socio-environmental governance issues in the Andes-Amazon region.

Ability and willingness to travel periodically, work occasional non-traditional hours, and participate in field activities in variable and sometimes remote conditions.


Preferred Qualifications:

PhD in a relevant discipline.

Experience with participatory mapping or co-production of spatial knowledge with community or Indigenous partners.

Experience with machine learning or GeoAI, image classification, ecological modeling, LiDAR, radar, drone or multispectral imagery, or automated monitoring workflows.

Experience developing web maps, dashboards, interactive decision-support tools, or other accessible geospatial applications.

Record of contributing to peer-reviewed publications, applied research products, or high-impact conservation plans and proposals.

FAA Remote Pilot Certificate.

Resume or curriculum vitae.

Cover letter describing relevant experience and interest in the position.

Portfolio with at least two examples of maps, geospatial analyses, spatial data visualizations, dashboards, or decision-support products.

Description
Mission San Juan Safaris (SJS) and San Juan Outfitters (SJO) are dedicated to sharing knowledge of the environment in hopes to encourage guests to develop a lifelong love of wildlife and its habitat and fostering marine stewardship. Our priorities are safety, education, and fun. 
San Juan Safaris and Outfitters uphold high industry standards in professionalism, knowledge, and experience. We strive to be the leaders in our field and hope to continue to achieve this through the expertise and enthusiasm of our staff.  
San Juan Safaris (SJS) and San Juan Outfitters (SJO) are within the upper echelon of the whale and wildlife watching companies in the Pacific Northwest: from the way our Captains drive out on the water, to the deep, meaningful connections that our staff forge with our guests. 


OFFICIAL JOB DESCRIPTION  
SUMMARY 
Perform daily whale and wildlife tours. Captain is responsible for safe operation and safety features, basic maintenance, accurate logs, overseeing Deckhand/Naturalist duties and setting a good example for wildlife viewing ethics and methods on the water. 
Steer and operate vessels using equipment such as radar, depth finders, radios, buoys, lights, and lighthouses. Follow daily weather and tidal conditions, port procedures, and current maritime laws/ rules of the road. Captains must have interpersonal skills and are responsible for communicating courteously and efficiently with all crew members in various situations out on the water and at port.
Season: May to October. Must be available on Saturdays, Sundays, evenings, and holidays. 

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
Operate the company vessels and conduct regular daily whale and wildlife tours. 
Perform ethical and responsible wildlife viewing practices. 
Finding and identifying various forms of marine life 
Oversee all operations and upkeep onboard the vessel while on duty, including navigation, maintenance, and compliance with local regulations; ensure the seaworthiness of the ship before every departure. 
Oversee First Mate duties. 
Maintain a high standard of quality for our tours. 
Maintain positive relationships and communications with staff. 
Abide by Pacific Whale Watch Association (PWWA) ([https://about:blank/]www.pacificwhalewatch.org/guidelines) Best Practices Guidelines for wildlife viewing. 
Adhere to company standards. 
Maintain a daily ship's log; Maintain all onboard equipment, and keep detailed records of daily activities, personnel reports, ship positions and movements, ports of call, weather conditions, passenger and cargo status and pollution control efforts. 
Provide oversight on all safety issues; instruct all new crewmembers in safety procedures. 
Alter navigation plans based on weather conditions to keep vessels and passengers safe; compute positions, set courses and determine speeds using charts, compasses, sextants, area plotting sheets and knowledge of local conditions. 

QUALIFICATIONS 
2+ years of experience as a Captain 
Firm knowledge of marine craft communication, signaling and navigation systems 
Strong single and twin-screw propulsion boat handling skills 
Detail oriented and safety-oriented work ethic. 
Must be team oriented and enjoy working with others; develop and build teams. 
Capable of working long/flexible hours and available weekends, evenings, and holidays throughout the summer 
Ability to comfortably lift 50 pounds and safely stand and move around on a dynamic moving platform for 5-10 hours a day. 

REQUIREMENTS: 
100-ton USCG Master License 
Must adhere to company dress code. 
Must have current First Aid/AED/CPR Certification through a reputable, nationally recognized organization. 
Valid Driver’s License and Passport 
Current WDFW Operators License 
Must have a current [https://about:blank/]Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) 
Subject to pre-employment and/or random drug testing 
Working phone with available voicemail 
Access to the Homebase App for schedule updates and the PWWA App for on water operations 
Non-smoker 
Reliable transportation 

BASIC EXPECTATIONS 
Well versed on local & federal laws regarding wildlife viewing. Must be familiar with the PWWA guidelines and No-Go Zones/wildlife sanctuaries and adhere to them strictly. The state and local governments have instituted laws that further protect all whales in the area. San Juan Safaris is serious about setting a good example for viewing etiquette. The techniques necessary to observe whales without interfering with their life processes take time to learn and requires additional skills apart from just captaining a boat.  
Must be familiar with the Marine Mammal Protection Act, NOAA Regulations, and regulations varying between United States and Canadian waters. 
Captains are expected to stay up to date on the latest research, regulations, and information regarding the Salish Sea Ecosystem. 
Background in ecotourism preferred, special training in marine ecology recommended. The position is for a dedicated person who understands and respects marine mammals and our company's philosophy. 
Able to easily multi-task, including performing administrative duties. 
Ability to maintain a professional, well-groomed appearance per company standards and expected to be in uniform while on the clock and in front of guests. 
Captains will be punctual when arriving at the boat and boarding guests. 
Captains are expected to check in with the reservations desk on the morning of scheduled shifts for any last-minute updates. Additionally, maintaining consistent, clear, and respectful communication with the manager of vessel operations as well as the port captain.
No photography or personal cell phone use while on duty. 

PAY & BENEFITS 
Starting pay $30 - $35 per hour (depending on experience), plus good tips. Work in a world-class outdoor marine environment with likeminded people and abundant wildlife. Discounts on outdoor gear, Riptide Cafe, and local restaurants. Free whale watching and kayaking on a "space available" basis, discounts for family and friends. 
All interested applicants please include a PDF cover letter, resume, and the contact information for three professional references.

 [email removed] and [email removed]

Description
We are seeking one field technician for muskrat and deer drone surveys in Illinois. These projects are operating through the Center for Wildlife and Sustainability Research at Southern Illinois University in collaboration with the Illinois Department of Natural Resources. The research technician will work directly with SIU graduate students on two different research projects. 

Project 1- Muskrats 
This project involves using sign surveys and drone surveys to determine if muskrats are present at a variety of sites around the state. The aim of this study is to evaluate the validity of using drones as a method for muskrat surveying and answering other questions regarding muskrat habitat choice in Illinois. The technician will be responsible for acting as visual observer for drone flights, conducting sign surveys on foot, and data entry. Operations for this projection will take place in December and February.  

Project 2- Deer 
This project involves comparing methods used to estimate white-tailed deer populations in Illinois. This position will primarily assist in drone surveys with responsibilities involving data entry and acting as a visual observer.  

Primary Responsibilities: 
Searching on foot for muskrat signs (tracks, huts, scat, etc.) 
Accurately collecting and processing data 
Acting as a visual observer for drone flights 
Operating 4wd university vehicles 

Location: 
Surveying will take place across the state of Illinois and will require some overnight travel to field sites. Housing will be provided in Carbondale, IL.

Starting at $16/hr. Maximum 37.5 hours/week. This position will run November 30th, 2026, through late February 2027, with time off for Christmas (exact dates to be determined). Fieldwork will primarily be conducted Mon – Friday with potential for changes depending on weather and site location.

Valid U.S. driver’s license 
Willingness to work long hours and outdoors in adverse weather conditions

Ability to spend multiple hours in the car each day travelling to field sites 
Strong communication skills 
Attention to detail 
Ability to navigate using GPS  
Obtained or working towards a bachelor’s degree in biology, ecology, wildlife, or related field 
Prior experience operating UAVs (drones) or FAA part 107 certification is a plus but not required.
