Description
Nokuse Land Conservancy is seeking an Avian Conservation Biologist to lead and continue development of its bird monitoring, research, and conservation across the property. Nokuse is a 56,000-acre ecological restoration project encompassing longleaf pine savanna, wetlands, bottomland hardwood forests, waterways, and other habitats important to southeastern wildlife.

This position combines field biology, applied research, data analysis, and conservation planning. The Avian Conservation Biologist will maintain established long-term monitoring efforts while also developing new projects that address questions relevant to bird conservation and habitat restoration at Nokuse. 

We are looking for someone who is comfortable working independently and taking ownership of a growing program. The successful candidate should be able to move a project from an initial ecological question through study design, field implementation, analysis, and communication of results. There is considerable opportunity to develop new research, build collaborations, and use findings to directly inform management on the property.

The appointment is for one year, with the possibility of extension for a candidate who is a good long-term fit for Nokuse.

Primary Responsibilities:

Avian Monitoring and Research

Lead and further develop Nokuse’s Long-term avian monitoring program using a combination pf passive acoustic monitoring and traditional field methods. Current work includes a fixed network of autonomous recording units (ARUs), point counts, transects, behavioral monitoring, and targeted surveys across a variety of habitats.

Responsibilities will include:

·       Deploying and maintaining ARUs and managing and analyzing acoustic data.
·       Continuing long-term monitoring of Nokuse bird community and seasonal studies, including ongoing work examining bird use across pine stands that differ in management condition. i.e. Overwintering habitat use.
·       Conducting standardized point counts, transects, and targeted surveys for focal species and habitats.
·       Expanding monitoring in wetlands, bottomland hardwood forests, pine savannas, creeks, and other aquatic systems. Some fieldwork will involve kayaking and boats to access remote areas.
·       Expanding avian monitoring on a recently acquired island property and using those data to help establish management priorities.
·       Maintaining organized long-term datasets and refining existing methods as monitoring objectives evolve.
·       Developing new studies when ecological or management questions arise.

Red-cockaded Woodpecker Reintroduction

Nokuse has completed substantial habitat and logistical preparation for the establishment of Red-cockaded Woodpeckers (RCWs), with translocation anticipated in 2027. The Avian Conservation Biologist will take a lead role in monitoring and developing this program following release:

·       Monitoring translocated birds to document retention, survival, group composition, territory establishment, and reproductive success.
·       Coordinating individual identification and banding efforts.
·       Monitoring artificial cavities and coordinating installation of additional cavities as the population expands.
·       Maintaining spatial and demographic records for the population.
·       Evaluating habitat conditions within existing and potential RCW territories and working with land management staff to identify future expansion areas.
·       Coordinating with state and federal agencies and completing required monitoring and reporting.
·       Maintaining relationships with regional RCW biologists and partners, including participation in the annual Southeastern Regional Translocation Cooperative (SRTC) meeting.
·       Communicating Nokuse’s progress and assisting with efforts to receive additional translocated birds as the population develops.

Applied Bird Conservation and Habitat Management

A major goal of Nokuse’s bird program is to use monitoring data to evaluate restoration outcomes and improve habitat management.

The Avian Conservation Biologist will work with Nokuse’s land management staff to assess bird community responses to prescribed fire, forest and hydrological restoration, and other management activities. The biologist will be expected to interpret monitoring results in an applied conservation context and make habitat management recommendations when supported by the data.

Attention will be given to species associated with healthy southeastern ecosystems and species of conservation concern, including Bachman’s Sparrow, Henslow’s Sparrow, Red-headed Woodpecker, Swallow-tailed Kite, Red-cockaded Woodpecker, among others.

The biologist will also maintain spatial records of rare or listed bird observations and identify emerging monitoring, research, or management needs.

Research Partnerships and Special Projects

Nokuse collaborates with universities, agencies, nonprofit organizations, and independent researchers. Current avian partnerships include work with the Stoddard Bird Lab at Tall Timbers Research Station and the Sam Shine Foundation on Bachman’s Sparrows, Henslow’s Sparrows, and other southeastern bird species.

The Avian Conservation Biologist will serve as the primary on-site contact for avian research projects and may assist with field logistics, bird capture and banding, telemetry, etc.

This position also includes four weeks of fieldwork in Indiana each year with the Sam Shine Foundation. Work may include Prairie Warbler mist-netting, banding, tagging, Motus and telemetry work, Cerulean Warbler BirdScape projects, and other bird related work. 

It is encouraged that the biologist will continue to develop independent and collaborative research questions using Nokuse’s monitoring programs and restoration landscape, with the goal of producing meaningful conservation results and, where appropriate, presentations or peer-reviewed publications.

Data, GIS, and Telemetry

This position includes use of ArcGIS Pro and R as regular components of study design, spatial analysis, data management, statistical analysis, visualization, and communication of results.

The biologist will also be responsible for maintaining Nokuse’s Motus Wildlife Tracking System, including routine station checks, troubleshooting power systems, receivers and sensor stations, and assisting with expansion of the network where appropriate.

Program Leadership and Communication

This position requires a high degree of independence and initiative. Nokuse staff and research partners will provide support, but the Avian Conservation Biologist should be comfortable identifying needs, developing projects, seeking appropriate expertise or partnerships, and carrying work through to completion.

Additional responsibilities may include:

·       Training or supervising seasonal technicians and other field personnel involved in avian projects.
·       Preparing quarterly, annual, and project specific summaries and reports.
·       Completing state and federal reporting associated with permitted or protected species work.
·       Presenting results to conservation organizations, research partners, professional groups, and scientific conferences.
·       Communicating monitoring results and management recommendations to Nokuse staff.
·       Supporting occasional outreach and social media content related to Nokuse’s bird conservation work.
·       Maintaining productive relationships with agency biologists, researchers, nonprofit partners, and other collaborators.

Qualifications

Required

·       Bachelor’s degree in wildlife biology, ecology, natural resources, or a related field.
·       At least two field seasons or equivalent professional experience conducting avian fieldwork.
·       Strong ability to identify birds by sight and sound. Familiarity with southeastern U.S. bird communities is strongly preferred.
·       Experience managing biological data and maintaining accurate field records.
·       Working knowledge of GIS and quantitative analysis, with the ability and willingness to develop greater proficiency in ArcGIS Pro and R.
·       Ability to work independently, organize multiple projects, and adapt field and research plans as conditions change.
·       Valid driver’s license.

Preferred

·       Master’s degree in wildlife biology, ecology, natural resources, or a related field.
·       Autonomous recording units and analysis of passive acoustic data.
·       Bird capture, mist-netting, handling, and banding.
·       Red-cockaded Woodpecker monitoring and management.
·       Ecological understanding of / experience working embedded in the longleaf pine       ecosystem.
·       Habitat assessment, prescribed fire ecology, or restoration ecology.
·       Radio telemetry, Motus, or other automated wildlife tracking systems. 
·       Ecological study design and analysis of long-term monitoring data.
·       ArcGIS Pro, spatial analysis, and field data collection applications.
·       Statistical analysis and visualization in R.
·       Scientific writing, technical reporting, and professional presentations.
·       Coordination with universities, state or federal agencies, nonprofit organizations, or other research partners.

Compensation

·       Hourly salary will be $20.00-$22.00/hour [MW1] depending on experience. 
·       A vehicle will be provided for field work.
·       Housing on or near the property is also provided as part of this position.

Successful Applicants will be interviewed in November, expected start date in January. To apply please send a CV, cover letters, and at least two references. Submit materials to [email removed]

Title- Wetland Permitting Specialist
Classification- Environmental Planner 3
Job Status- Full-Time/Permanent
WDFW Program- Capital and Asset Management Program (CAMP)
Duty Station- Olympia, Washington – Thurston County
Hybrid/Telework- The selected candidate may be able to telework up to two days per week at the discretion of the supervisor.

Learn more about being a member of Team WDFW!


Play a critical part in advancing construction and capital projects by delivering the wetland science and regulatory support required to secure environmental permits.

Through hands-on fieldwork, technical analysis, and close coordination with permitting teams and regulatory agencies, the position ensures wetland impacts are accurately assessed, mitigation strategies are developed, and compliance requirements are met.


What to Expect:
Among the varied range of responsibilities held within this role, the Wetland Permitting Specialist will,

Guide wetland delineations, mapping, rating, report writing, and mitigation requirements for CAMP projects:
Develop, plan, and coordinate activities associated with wetland delineation preparation. Research, analyze, and record data about the project site.
Perform fieldwork for wetland delineations throughout the state using an Arrow GPS unit and iPad with Field Maps. Analyze soils, vegetation, and hydrology on site.
Complete data forms and wetland rating forms during and after field activities.
Draft, prepare, and submit wetland delineation reports and mitigation plans for the preparation of permit application packages. 
Determine eligibility of consultants to perform work for the agency and recommend the selection of those qualified for state planning. 

Assist lead permitting staff with environmental tasks in work areas:
Perform seining, sampling, and removal of aquatic species from active construction areas.
Perform water quality sampling including pH, turbidity, and dissolved oxygen, or other site samples.

Prepare additional supporting permit documents for policy and regulatory compliance:
Serve as a technical liaison while coordinating with planning personnel in WDFW and other state departments to determine site constraints, local requirements, and wetland delineation requirements for projects.
Prepare Biological Assessments and Evaluations, Habitat Management Plans, Mitigation Plans, and other biological documents required for permitting.
Maintain knowledge of current environmental regulations.
 

Working Conditions:

Work Setting, including hazards: Duties are performed in an office setting and at construction and field sites, including in-water work which requires adhering to safety protocol and utilizing personal protective equipment (PPE). Work in inclement weather, walk on uneven terrain including slippery footing, mud, steep slopes, and other challenging field conditions for extended periods. Climb ladders, work from boats, and from elevated locations. This position may involve working in or near water, including tasks that require navigating, negotiating, and performing duties related to water environments.

Schedule: Typically, 40 hours per week, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Workload may require additional hours, and the work schedule may require adjustments to meet business needs. A flexible work schedule may be considered, subject to supervisory approval.

Travel Requirements: Travel throughout the state using an agency-provided vehicle for fieldwork will be required, with long field days and overnight stays likely to occur. Travel may occur on weekends in rare circumstances. Additional travel throughout the state to attend training, meetings, and conferences may occur.

Tools and Equipment: Pickup trucks, computer hardware and software, cell phone/iPad, Arrow GPS unit, Field Maps, ArcGIS Pro/Online, and field sampling equipment (including a shovel, turbidity meter, pH meter, conductivity meter, and fish removal equipment).

Customer Interactions: May interact with members of the public while accessing work areas or attending public meetings/hearings.


Qualifications:

Required Qualifications:

Professional experience in wetland science, habitat management or research, natural resource planning, or an equivalent field may be substituted for the required education on a year-by-year basis.


Option 1:
An Associate’s degree with an emphasis/specialty in wetland science, natural resource science, water resource management, environmental science, environmental policy, or a related field.
And 
Four (4) years of professional experience in wetland science, natural resource planning, federal, state, and local permitting, or an equivalent field.

Option 2:
A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in wetland science, natural resource science, water resource management, environmental science, environmental policy, or an equivalent field.
And 
Two (2) years of professional experience in wetland science, natural resource planning, federal, state, and local permitting, or an equivalent field.

Option 3:
Two (2) years of experience as an Environmental Planner 2.

Certifications/Licenses:
Valid Driver’s License.

 Preferred Qualifications:
In addition to the required qualifications, our ideal applicant will possess some or all the following:

Experience with:
The Washington Tool for Online Rating (WATOR).

Knowledge Competencies:
Western and Eastern Washington wetland plant identification.
Western and Eastern Washington Wetland Rating.
Data processing and analysis using Esri ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and Field Maps.
Vegetative surveys and monitoring.
Hydric soil identification.
Ordinary High Water Mark (OHWM) identification and delineation.
Aquatic species protection methodology and implementation.

Skill and Ability Competencies:
Scientific/technical report writing and review.
Code, law, and regulation research and interpretation.
Field work techniques and safety.
Field data collection, entry, and analysis.
 

Your application must include the following:
A completed online application showcasing how your qualifications align with the job requirements.
An up-to-date resume.
A cover letter detailing your interest in the position, your relevant skills and experience, and why you are the ideal candidate.
At least three professional references with current contact information.
Writing Exercise: Candidates selected for an interview will be asked to complete a job-related writing exercise. This exercise will involve reviewing provided field notes and data sheets and then providing a scientific writing sample describing site conditions and wetland characteristics.

Job Description
Position Summary:
The Postdoctoral Researcher in Human–Wildlife Interactions will investigate how dynamic patterns of human activity shape wildlife behavior, habitat use, and landscape connectivity. The position offers an opportunity to integrate large human mobility datasets with ongoing and completed wildlife studies across the United States, linking fine-scale behavioral responses with broader patterns of habitat availability and connectivity. 

The Postdoctoral Researcher will work closely with Dr. Mark Ditmer (USFS Rocky Mountain Research Station & CSU); Dr. Philip Manlick (USFS Pacific Northwest Research Station), and Dr. George Wittemyer (CSU) to develop innovative approaches and questions involving the influence of human activities and disturbance.

Full Consideration Date: December 1, 2026

The Department of Fish, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology at Colorado State University seeks a highly motivated researcher with expertise in spatial ecology. Based within the Department of Fish, Wildlife, and Conservation Biology, this position will contribute to expanding the frontiers of knowledge through broad-based expertise in applied ecology, quantitative methods, and the human dimensions of fish and wildlife conservation and management.

The successful candidate will conduct independent and collaborative research focused on spatial ecology and the application of advanced analytical approaches to conservation and wildlife management challenges.

Essential Job Duties:
Conduct independent and collaborative research using spatial and spatiotemporal data to address conservation and wildlife management challenges.
Develop and apply quantitative methods and analytical approaches to ecological and conservation research.
Analyze, interpret, and communicate research findings through scientific publications, presentations, and technical reports.
Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams across ecology, conservation, natural resources, and related fields.
Contribute to the advancement of knowledge in applied ecology, quantitative methods, and the human dimensions of fish and wildlife conservation and management.

Conditions of Employment:
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States by the proposed start date. Colorado State University will not provide visa sponsorship for this position.
Must be able to work effectively both independently and as part of a collaborative research team.
Must be able to travel as required to conduct research and attend professional meetings.

Supervision:
May provide guidance, training, or mentoring to graduate students, undergraduate students, or research personnel associated with project activities.

Minimum Qualifications:
Ph.D. degree in a pertinent biological, physical, or computer science field.
Demonstrated research focus on spatial ecology.
Strong publication record in spatial ecology.
Experience with research design in field settings.

Preferred Qualifications:
Demonstrated proficiency in movement analyses, analysis of camera data, spatial statistical modeling, and/or processing of large datasets.
Demonstrated ability to develop and apply Geographic Information Systems (GIS) methods and tools.
Demonstrated proficiency with scientific computing and programming languages, such as MATLAB, R, Python, or similar languages used in research applications.
Research experience examining wildlife responses to human activity or environmental change.
Demonstrated experience working in collaborative research settings.

Description
Wildlife Monitoring Technician – Generalists and Bird Specialists

Iowa State University 

Locations: Boone, Sioux City, Iowa City, IA

Tentative Locations: Waterloo and Indianola, IA 

Closing Date: Applications received by November 30th will receive priority review and interviews will be conducted in early December.  

Generalist Wildlife monitoring technicians (~20) and bird specialists (~5) are needed to help with Iowa’s Multiple Species Inventory and Monitoring (MSIM) program. Applicants will work as part of a 5-person research and monitoring team to collect information on birds, mammals, reptiles, amphibians, fish, and insects on public lands. Field work for all positions will be conducted throughout the state of Iowa with significant travel during the workday.

Specific job duties include (but are not limited to) identifying, handling, and marking small mammals, amphibians, reptiles, and fish; maintaining a variety of traps for small mammals, amphibians, reptiles, and fish; conducting surveys for and handling butterflies and odonates; identifying and measuring plant species; data entry; deploying bat acoustic detectors; and assisting with other tasks as needed. 

Bird specialists will primarily conduct bird point count surveys using visual and auditory cues, and butterfly and bumblebee surveys. There will be opportunities to also assist the crew in the duties mentioned above.

Check out this video to see what past technicians have worked on: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hytd3YuVeZ0.

Positions are temporary, full-time (40 hours/week) starting March 22nd and ending October 15th, 2027. Applicants available for the full field season are strongly encouraged to apply. Candidates available from mid-May through October 15th, 2027, as well as a limited number of summer-only applicants available from mid-May through August 2027, will also be considered. Salary is $14-18/hr dependent upon qualifications and relevant experience. No overtime will be provided. Vehicles will be provided for work-related travel. Field housing is available to rent for the Sioux City crew. 

 

 Minimum Qualifications:
Applicants should be graduated from, currently enrolled in, or on break between semesters of college with a degree in (or pursuing a degree in) wildlife ecology, biology, or a closely related natural resource field 
Applicants must have the physical ability to work long hours outdoors, walk long distances, carry field equipment in rough terrain, and wade through water 
Must be able to work independently and as part of a team 
Must be able to work during diverse weather conditions and on weekends, holidays, nights, and evenings as required
Must have a strong work ethic and attention to detail
If needed, must be able to travel overnight for work-related duties
Applicants must be at least 18 years old, possess a valid driver’s license, and pass an Iowa motor vehicle check to be able to drive a state vehicle
Additional requirements for bird specialists:
Able to identify Midwest bird species by sight and sound
Comfortable working early mornings and driving several hours alone

Preferred qualifications:
Possess a B.S. degree in wildlife ecology, biology or a related field
Experience with at least one taxonomic group (mammals, birds, herptiles, fish, mussels, odonates, butterflies, or plants) 

How to Apply:
Complete applications must include a resume/CV with contact information for 3 references and a cover letter that clearly states position of interest (generalist or bird specialist), crew preference(s), and start date. 
 Please submit applications here: 
https://isu.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/ConfidentialOpenSearchWaiver/job/Remote---Iowa/Wildlife-Monitoring-Technician---Temporary_R20127
 

Questions can be emailed to the MSIM team at [email removed].

Description
The Sheth plant evolutionary ecology lab in the Department of Plant and Microbial Biology at North Carolina State University (Raleigh, NC) is currently seeking 1-2 enthusiastic field technicians to participate in an NSF-funded study (https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=2220928&HistoricalAwards=false) under the direction of Dr. Seema Sheth and in collaboration with Drs. Susana Wadgymar (Davidson College), Jill Anderson (University of Georgia), Megan DeMarche (University of Georgia), and Emily Josephs (Michigan State University). The project combines approaches from evolutionary biology, field ecology, and population genomics in a broadly distributed native plant species (Chamaecrista fasciculata, Fabaceae) to forecast population dynamics range-wide under climate change. The technician will be part of a dynamic, dedicated, and engaged research group as well as a member of a multidisciplinary and multi-institution collaborative group that includes Botanic Garden and conservation professionals.

Dates: February 1, 2027 through November 30, 2027 (exact dates flexible) 

Expected duties: The successful candidate will contribute to a collaborative study of eco-evolutionary responses to climate in the partridge pea, Chamaecrista fasciculata, an annual legume that grows in disturbed habitats in central and eastern North America. The technician’s primary responsibilities involve collaborating with the PIs and other researchers to establish and maintain a large common garden experiment and to collect data from ~6,000 transplanted seeds at Mason Farm Biological Reserve in Chapel Hill, NC. This work includes preparing seeds for planting, planting seeds, setting up the garden infrastructure, building open-top chambers, collecting data on traits and fitness, entering data, maintenance tasks in the garden (e.g., weeding), processing samples in the lab, and communicating with Dr. Sheth and other team members. The technician will also have opportunities to train and mentor undergraduate students and work with graduate students.

Required qualifications
Previous experience with field research in ecology, evolution, and/or botany
Bachelor’s degree in ecology, evolutionary biology, botany, or a related field
Valid US driver’s license
Ability to work outdoors in challenging conditions for long days
Previous experience with field research in ecology, evolution, and/or botany
Attention to detail; precise, neat work; ability to perform repetitive tasks
Excellent problem-solving and communication skills

Preferred qualifications
Coursework in ecology, plant biology, genetics, or related fields
Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 lbs
Desire to train and mentor other team members
Comfortable with manual labor, including but not limited to using common tools, light carpentry, and gardening/landscaping techniques
Experience with troubleshooting in the field

Commitment to field safety: We are committed to providing a safe field work experience for all members of the collaborative team. We are happy to discuss and address any safety-related concerns you have.

About NC State and the Raleigh area: NC State’s Department of Plant and Microbial Biology offers a highly-rated research environment and is situated in a collaborative and scientifically stimulating atmosphere in the Research Triangle, with both UNC Chapel Hill and Duke University nearby. Raleigh is a lively yet affordable city with a high standard of living, and its surroundings offer numerous recreational activities.

Review of applications will begin on November 10 and continue until the position is filled. Due to the large volume of applicants, we will not be able to respond to individual emails about this position or meet with applicants prior to submission of application materials. 

Contact
Seema Sheth

Certified Conservation Planner
Location: DelAtlantic Conservation District, Mays Landing, NJ

Qualifications: 

NRCS Level 3 Certified Conservation Planner status (Certified Crop Advisor or NRCS Level 2 Conservation Planner status will be considered) Submit proof of certification and Job Approval Authority

Graduate of an accredited college with a Bachelor’s Degree in Agriculture, Forestry, Natural Sciences, Resource Management, Environmental Studies or related areas of study. 

A valid New Jersey driver’s license is required

Job Description: 

This position is located at the DelAtlantic Conservation District (DACD) Office. DelAtlantic Conservation District works in cooperation with the New Jersey State Agriculture Development Committee (SADC) to provide technical and financial assistance to preserved farm landowners to encourage the implementation of conservation practices designed to address natural resource issues. The Planner is responsible for customer communication, conservation planning, program contracting, outreach and technical assistance under the direction of the Senior Ag. Conservationist. 

Major duties include:

Independently completes Resource Concern evaluations according to NRCS and SADC standards

Independently develops Resource Management System (RMS) level Conservation Plans for preserved farms in accordance with NRCS and SADC standards

Independently document and certify conservation practices for which Job Approval Authority is held

Learn and understand SADC policies regulating financial assistance programs 

Assist other staff who lack Conservation Planner Certification

Determines need and site location, survey and designs, stakes out and supervises installation of contracted conservation practices

Communicate with team members, farmers, and private landowners in person, over the phone and through written communication

Make initial contact with landowners and provide technical assistance in the layout, installation, and maintenance of conservation practices called for in plans and contracts

Calculates soil loss and provides soil loss data for computation of water quality benefits. Reports number and acres of land benefited from planning and application of conservation practices.

Applies a working knowledge of soil and water quality planning and designing to explain its purpose and intent, to answer questions, and to explain benefits of improved land use and water quality.

Follows up in writing and by field visit on conservation practices, with landowners to encourage and arrange for proper maintenance and to schedule application of additional practices called for in contracts. Records the kind of technical assistance needed and when it is scheduled or when contact should be made to develop firm schedule. Notes changes in practice installation dates, items to be added or deleted, changes in farming operations, etc. Documents that all items previously applied are being properly maintained using accountability tools.

Maintains records and assists in the preparation of reports on work planned and accomplished.

Achieves/Maintains NRCS Level 3 Conservation Planner Certification by completing continuing education requirements

Continue to earn Job Approval Authority for additional practices

Offer input to Senior Ag. Conservationist for future program opportunities

Serves as an incidental motor vehicle operator. This requires the operation of a motor vehicle on both public and private roads during daylight hours and occasionally after dark. A valid New Jersey driver’s license is required.

Actively supports and participates in the safety and health program activities as required. Complies with all appropriate safety and health rules and regulations in the performance of assigned tasks.

Actively supports the Equal Opportunity and Civil Rights Program and assures the delivery of agency programs and services are carried out in accordance with policy and procedures without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, age, or physical or mental handicap.

Complies with and adheres to all Federal and State policies and policies of the DelAtlantic Soil Conservation District. The specialist will be supervised by the Senior Ag. Conservationist and the District Manager. 

Requires being able to work outdoors in most weather conditions and to be able to walk over uneven, soft, and/or wet ground. Occasionally lifting/moving equipment or materials up to 50lbs may be required. 

Other duties as assigned by Senior Ag. Conservationist and/or the DACD District Manager.

Interested applicants are encouraged to submit a resume and cover letter outlining your interest, along with a list of references, to:

Description
Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission is recruiting candidates who are highly motivated and detail oriented to fill a Fishery Biologist position to assist with leading a field survey crew operating rotary screw traps on both the Lower American and Sacramento Rivers.
 
The survey season extends from December through June and the position will be full-time, seasonal and based in Sacramento, CA. In collaboration with the Supervisory Fishery Biologist, the Biologist will supervise crew members while conducting daily field activities and data collection using rotary screw traps to monitor the emigration of juvenile Chinook Salmon.
 
This will include but is not limited to identifying various fish species, assessing life stage and run, collecting environmental data, and maintaining field equipment. The candidate will demonstrate safety consciousness and train crew members on all safety and data collection protocols. The candidate must be able to conduct physically challenging field work in potentially stressful situations, all while maintaining a positive attitude and encouraging crew members to do the same. The candidate must be willing to work in inclement weather and be willing to work weekends and overtime. This position will require working with multiple agencies, technicians, and biologists, so having good interpersonal skills are required. Together with the Supervisory Fishery Biologist, the Biologist will help compile and analyze data, develop annual reports, and maintain proper scientific collecting permits.
 
Duties and responsibilities include:
Lead and manage a 2-3 person crew in daily field operations
Operate and maintain 16 and 18 foot motorized water craft and 4WD trucks
Operate and maintain 8-foot tandem rotary screw traps
Identify, handle, anesthetize, and collect biological data from juvenile fish species
Handle endangered or threatened fish species according to permits and protocols
Assist with daily QA/QC of data
Maintain proper scientific collecting permits
Develop monthly and annual reports
 

Mandatory Qualifications:

Must be able to lift 50 lbs.
Ability to swim 50 yards and tread water for 10 minutes
Ability to communicate efficiently and provide oral and written directions
Knowledge of fishery biology (including fish species identification skills)
Knowledge of computer applications and software (Excel, Access, Word, Outlook, R)
Knowledge of writing technical reports
Must be able to read, write, and speak English
Ability to identify juvenile Chinook Salmon and Steelhead
Must be comfortable working from, operating, and trailering motorized watercraft
Must have a valid driver’s license with a clean driving record
Previous supervisory or crew lead experience
Knowledge of Salmonid biology and life history
Juvenile fish trapping and handling experience
Knowledge of mark-recapture methods and theory
Ability to operate and trailer a motorized watercraft
Essential Functions:
(The functions listed below are characteristic of the type and level of work associated with this group and pay band. They are not all-inclusive. Individual positions may perform some or all, as well as other similar work under close to general supervision.)

Lead and participate in survey crews that conduct fishery presence/absence research, recreational/commercial fishing surveys, anadromous fish escapement surveys (carcass, redd, trap/weir, snorkel, etc.), or tag detection and mark recovery surveys.
Make standardized observations such as species identification, length, weight, behavior, growth, survival, reproductive condition, and/or signs of parasites, diseases or pathogens, fin clips or tags.
Lead and perform data entry for data from recovered tags, representative biological samples, telemetry devices, oceanographic data, fish tickets, commercial landing estimates, logbooks, scale cards, port sampling, onboard observers, etc.
Error check the data, maintain and update database, analyze and organize data in the appropriate format (table, spreadsheet, memorandum, or report) necessary for transfer to individuals, agencies, and organizations. Modify software programs and perform data queries. Prepare summary reports to transfer data.
Assist researchers in investigations of long term and short term fisheries resource management problems. Collect biological samples, record data, perform routine analyses of data, and contribute draft sections to scientific papers for publication.
Assist in design, development, and installation of components of naturalistic environments. Assist with analysis of the behavior of different species in simulated environments. Videotape, photograph, and record data for characteristics such as growth, health, fitness, social activity, reproductive success, foraging success, and anti-predator behavior.
Establish and direct sport, commercial, hatchery, and natural spawn sampling and bio-sampling protocols to best meet data requirements.
Knowledge Required by the Position:
At the lower end of the range, employees use knowledge of basic arithmetic, reading, writing, and data collection to perform routine or repetitive tasks.
At the upper end of the position range, employees use knowledge of the basic principles and protocols of fish biology to make readings, measurements, and observations; execute tests; collect samples, etc. If complex equipment systems are operated, the employee has the knowledge to perform calibrations or adjustments to achieve desired results.


Physical Demands:
Demands can range from moderate -- where there is walking, climbing stairs and ladders, reaching, lifting, bending, and strenuous sweeping -- to rigorous. In the latter case, the incumbent must be able to handle buckets of water or gear weighing up to 50 pounds. Long daily periods of hiking, carrying equipment, swimming, and/or standing may be required. Some work requires the ability to maintain footing in fast-moving water.

 

Work Environment:
A portion of the work is performed in an office setting with adequate lighting, heating and ventilation. The majority is performed in fish processing labs, fish holding areas, and/or in the field. Incumbents may work on narrow, elevated walkways and platforms that are over or adjacent to water. Field work involves exposure to all types of weather, slippery rocks, trails, irregular terrain, insects, poison oak, rough or fast-moving water, or cold water temperatures. Work at high elevations or aboard boats may be required.


Qualifications
Minimum Qualification Requirements:
A range of education and experience may be presented.  At the lower end of the range, candidates must present successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that included a major in biological science with at least 6 semester hours in aquatic subjects and at least 12 semester hours in the animal sciences.  An equivalent combination of experience and education is also qualifying.
At the upper end of the range, candidates must present one year of Specialized Experience** OR a year of graduate education that is directly related to the work of the position.
**Specialized Experience is experience that equips the applicant with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position and is typically in or related to the work of the position being filled.  To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower level in the normal line of progression for the position being filled.

Description
Description
The Research Associate Program at GBI, in cooperation with the National Park Service (NPS) at Mojave National Preserve (MOJA), is recruiting one Desert Tortoise Technician to participate in wildlife surveys, resource monitoring, data collection, and natural resource management activities throughout the preserve.
As the field season is late in the year, the positions will not be exclusively focused on desert tortoises. Technicians may have opportunities to conduct tortoise monitoring for construction projects, along with a variety of other resource management activities, including desert spring surveys, bat emergence surveys using acoustic recorders and thermal cameras, and habitat improvement projects for the Mohave tui chub fish. These activities will provide opportunities to support the preservation and management of the preserve's diverse desert ecosystems and sensitive wildlife species.

Primary Responsibilities:

Monitor project areas during construction and other activities that could damage habitat or pose risks to endangered or threatened species, including opportunities for desert tortoise monitoring.
Conduct wildlife and natural resource surveys, potentially including desert spring surveys and bat emergence surveys using acoustic recorders and thermal cameras.
Assist with habitat improvement and management activities for sensitive species, including the Mohave tui chub fish.
Collect, organize, analyze, and manage wildlife observations and other natural resource datasets within and around MOJA.
Work collaboratively with project managers and NPS Resource Management staff to support ongoing conservation and monitoring efforts.
Assist with resource-based activities and monitoring park resources, sometimes in coordination with volunteers.
Help promote public understanding and appreciation of MOJA’s natural, cultural, historical, and recreational resources.

Timeline:

Early November 2026; Term length 7 weeks 
Full time (40 hours/week)
Schedule: Schedule: 4-10’s or 5, 4, 9’s (subject to change as needed)
 

Location:
Mojave National Preserve (MOJA) is 1.6 million acres, with about 44% of it designated as Wilderness. While most of MOJA is made up of the Mojave Desert, components of the Great Basin Desert are found in higher elevations and parts of the southern portion of the park are made up of the Sonoran Desert. Resources of the region include threatened and/or endangered species habitat, big game habitats, abandoned mine lands, and historic and prehistoric cultural sites.


Compensation and Benefits:
Compensation: $22.50 hourly;
Benefits: 

Company-paid comprehensive medical, dental (with option to upgrade in coverage), and vision insurance;
$25,000 Basic Life & AD&D insurance at no cost;
Access to Pro Deals;
Housing: Will be provided to the selected participant at no additional cost. The Park will provide housing in a dormitory. The interns will have a private room with a shared bath, shared kitchen and common areas, located in Essex, CA at the Hole-in-the-Wall Fire Center. 
 

Qualifications
Required:
●    Must meet the Public Land Corps Hiring Authority age and citizenship requirements (see more information in PLC section below);
●    Possess reliable vehicle or other form of transportation;
●    Possess a valid, state-issued driver’s license and clean driving record;
●    Previous experience monitoring on Mojave Desert tortoise projects or working with Mojave Desert tortoise;
●    Undergraduate or Graduate degree in Wildlife Management, Wildlife Biology, Natural Resources, or a closely related field in the biological sciences.
 

Preferred: 
●    Previous U.S. Fish and Wildlife approval as an Authorized Mojave Desert Tortoise Biologist, preferred;
●    Familiarity and knowledge of natural resource management at western National Parks, specifically wildlife;
●    Experience in performing field work, and applying methodological protocols for collecting field data;
●    Ability to work in extreme and remote parts of the park;
●    Familiarity with ecological processes and the fauna, as well as the flora, of the Mojave and/or Sonoran Deserts;
●    Familiarity with or previous experience working in the Mojave and/or Sonoran Deserts;
●    Experience operating 4WD trucks on paved and unpaved roads, unimproved roads;
●    Experience using hand-held GPS equipment for data collection and navigation;
●    Ability to read and navigate using topographic maps and a compass;
●    Experience using ArcGIS software; 
●    Knowledge or familiarity with Mojave National Preserve, preferred;
●    Ability to communicate effectively, both written and orally, with a diverse audience;
●    Willingness and ability to work, hike long distances carrying 40-50 pounds, and lift, carry and use equipment in harsh, variable desert conditions, including in extreme heat; and
●    Willingness to work a variable schedule, possibly including some weekends.
●    Ability to work independently to accomplish goals;
●    Ability to communicate effectively with team members, agency staff, and a diverse public;
●    Possess good organizational skills;
●    Possess a favorably adjudicated background clearance; and
●    Must be motivated, self-directed, organized, and detail oriented in order to balance multiple tasks simultaneously.


Successful applicants must complete a Department of Interior (DOI) Background Investigation (BI) or submit paperwork to NPS human resources indicating an active and fully adjudicated BI has already been completed prior to beginning position. If you already have a fully adjudicated BI, please let us know in your application.


Physical Demands:
The Wildlife Monitor will be required to hike and navigate rugged, steep terrain for extended periods, often carrying up to 50 lbs of gear. The position involves working in varying weather conditions, including temperatures ranging from 51°F to 100°F in summer and snow in winter. The technician will need to stand, kneel, crouch, or bend for long periods during surveys and equipment setup, as well as camp overnight in rustic conditions. The role also involves working in remote, high-altitude environments (6,500 ft) and driving safely on unpaved roads. The technician must be adaptable to physically demanding field conditions and be capable of working both independently and as part of a team, requiring flexibility, stamina, and focus.

Please apply online through this application link by submitting an up-to-date resume, one-page cover letter that details your interest in the position, and any qualifications not fully described in your resume, contact information for three professional and/or academic references. Be sure to complete any preliminary questions prompted in the application and sign your application.

Description
Civil Engineering Technician
Location: NRCS Field Office Woodstown, NJ
Classification: Full-time (35 hours/week)

INTRODUCTION
Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) and the DelAtlantic Conservation District have a shared and complimentary mission to assist land users to conserve their soil, water, and related natural resources.
The DelAtlantic Conservation District is a New Jersey state organization seeking to hire a civil engineering technician to work as a partner employee. The partner employee would be housed in the NRCS Woodstown field office serving both the Woodstown and Vineland field offices and perform tasks as assigned by the NRCS District Conservationist.
As an Engineering Technician (Civil) in the designated office at the field level, the primary responsibility is to design engineering practices, prepare engineering drawings, compute quantities, and assist field office personnel in the application of engineering practices.

MAJOR DUTIES
Technical Assistance (40%)
Provides engineering technical assistance for preliminary site investigations and conservation planning. Defines site limitations, design data, criteria, and applicable laws or regulations. Develops alternative solutions for solving complex resource management concerns in the areas of erosion control, water management, agricultural waste management, water quality and irrigation.
Provides quality control services including layout, material testing, and construction checks in order to ensure adherence to technical standards. Explains construction details to field office personnel, landowners, and contractors.
Prepared designs are reviewed and approved by NRCS for compliance with NRCS technical standards, accuracy of information, completeness, and feasibility of construction.
Provides technical guidance and direction to field office and district staff in the planning, design, and construction of engineering practices with supervision.
Surveys and Site Investigations (20%)
Assists with engineering design surveys, construction layout, and construction checks. Defines type of survey and detail and accuracy required to meet design and construction needs.
Based on field evaluations, determines the type, scope, and intensity of field investigations and surveys needed.

Design (20%)
Assists with collection of field data and assures adequacy of collected data. Sees that procedures and products conform to current NRCS policy and standards. Prepares site specific engineering designs, drawings, and specifications.
Performs drafting and other graphical work on a computer-aided drafting system. Maintains state-of-the-art knowledge in the use, application, and management of computer hardware and software applicable to available computer-aided drafting (CAD) systems. As necessary, trains others in the use of the system. Maintains the system equipment and the supplies for the system with supervision.
Documents layout and construction in conservation assistance notes or job diary. Documents completed work to higher graded supervisor or similar authority for certification and approval.
Computes quantities associated with projects designed in the field office. Exercises judgment in selecting and applying standard methods of computation for quantities such as concrete, earth fill, and excavation. Checks quantity computations made by others for accuracy and completeness.
From rough sketches provided by engineers, or other field office personnel, develops standard drawings for area use for a variety of conservation practices. Employee independently determines the layout of the standard drawings and details needed to adequately construct the practices. Standard drawings are developed on the CAD system.

Training (10%)
Supports engineering training needs for various field office personnel. Helps to provide engineering instruction in the use of the National Engineering Manual, the Engineering Field Handbook, Agricultural Waste Manual Field Handbook, State Technical Guide, and various technical releases and handbooks. Supports training in surveying and engineering equipment usage. Participates in training program for students and new technicians assigned to the duty station
Provides informal training and assists with formal training of field office personnel, district personnel, and others in the private sector in the technical aspects of soil and water conservation.
Engineering Quality Control (10%)
Coordinates with engineering specialists in performing NRCS quality reviews of conservation practices. Checks engineering work of field office personnel with supervision.

Other
Performs duties in a manner supportive of civil rights policy without regard to political affiliation, race, color, religion, sex, marital status, age, handicap, or national origin. Supports and participates in the broad spectrum of safety and health program activities. Complies with all appropriate safety and health rules and regulations in the performance of assigned tasks.

CONDITION OF EMPLOYMENT - Must possess and maintain a valid state motor vehicle operator's license for the type of vehicle(s) operated to perform the duties of this position. This will require the operation of a motor vehicle on both public and private roads during daylight hours and occasionally after dark.

Qualifications:
Knowledge of survey techniques, including use of electronic survey equipment, in order to independently gather field data, perform layout, verify construction of conservation practices and systems, and resolve difficult but well-precedented issues.
Knowledge of construction techniques, contracting procedures, and NRCS quality assurance policy in order to read plans and understand construction and material specifications.
Knowledge of construction safety policy and requirements in order to perform installation, testing, and maintenance duties.
Knowledge of NRCS engineering technical standards, methods, and procedures related to the investigation, design, and construction of conservation engineering practices in order to implement conservation practices.
Knowledge of NRCS policy and procedures related to the planning of conservation practices in order to assist in the development of conservation plans.
Knowledge of engineering-related computer systems, e.g. CAD systems and others, in order to prepare designs for conservation practices.
Ability to apply the fundamentals of mathematics, science, and engineering in order to design solutions to resource problems.
Ability to prepare concise construction drawings, including the use of computer assisted drafting techniques, in order to facilitate the construction of conservation practices.
Ability to work effectively with co-workers, contractors, partners, and landowners in order to provide for the efficient installation of conservation measures.
Thorough knowledge of the grammatical usage of the English language.
Ability to carry out work as directed.Ability to pass a Federal Background check and Employment Eligibility Verification
Must possess a valid New Jersey drivers license.

Education: Associates Degree or equivalent.
Recommended: Graduate of an accredited college with a Bachelor Degree or Associates Degree in Agriculture, Engineering, Natural Resource sciences or related field. Bachelor's degree should include at least 24 semester hours in any combination of courses such as engineering, engineering or industrial technology, construction, physics, drafting, surveying, physical science or mathematics. 6hrs of drafting is recommended.

Physical Demands:
Regular physical exertion in an outdoor setting is required. Walking long distances over rough terrain under a variety of weather conditions is to be expected. Sitting at a desk or drafting table for long periods of time is occasionally required. Driving to work assignments may take up to three hours one way.

Work Environment:
Work is often performed out-of-doors with regular exposure to heavy equipment, noise, adverse weather, and rough terrain. Protective equipment is necessary on construction sites. Exposure to farm animals, insects, and poisonous plants and snakes can be expected. Environment can vary from agricultural fields to the urban setting. Office work is performed in the Woodstown and Vineland NRCS Field Offices.

Terms of Employment:
Full-time position 35 hours per week
Salary - $52,500 per year
Insurance – Health, Rx, dental
Pension – NJ Public Employees Retirement System
Unemployment and Disability as per NJ State Policy
Position located at NRCS-Woodstown field office

How to Apply:
Interested applicants are encouraged to submit a resume and cover letter outlining your interest, along with a list of references, to:
Riley Blankenship, Senior Ag. Conservationist 
DelAtlantic Conservation District
6260 Old Harding Highway
Mays Landing, NJ 08330; 
or by email to Riley Blankenship at [email removed]

We strongly encourage all qualified professionals to apply. The DelAtlantic Conservation District is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of sex, race, age, national origin, ethnic background, disability or any other characteristic protected by law.

Description
Sequoia Ecological Consulting seeks a staff-first Technical Services Manager who is grounded in people-centered leadership and environmental consulting acumen to lead, support, and grow the team who protect California’s sensitive habitats, threatened species, and wild landscapes. 

Organization Background 

Sequoia Ecological Consulting is a certified woman-owned environmental consulting firm of about 70 people, headquartered in Walnut Creek with offices across Northern and Southern California. The firm provides biological services, regulatory permitting, and other environmental consulting services to public agencies, utilities, and private clients statewide, working on projects that shape California’s infrastructure, water, energy, and open space. 

Sequoia pairs statewide reach on high-impact projects with a close-knit culture where people know each other’s names. The culture is collaborative, high-performing, and professional. Sequoia is investing deliberately in how its people are supervised, developed, and supported so every technical staff member has a clear path for growth. 

Position Overview and Responsibilities 

Sequoia Ecological Consulting seeks a Technical Services Manager whose first job is people: the dedicated supervisor, advocate, and career-development lead for technical staff from the Project Manager tier through the newest field biologists, reporting to the Director of Technical Services. The role will take on the day-to-day people management that currently rests with the Principals, and it is central to building a team culture where staff feel supported, trusted, and able to grow. 

This position calls for a proven people leader with the consulting and technical credibility to make sound staffing and delivery decisions. The role supports project and program management and carries a small billable component to support the project teams.  

The Technical Services Manager will own staff supervision, performance management, career development, hiring, workload balance, and support for project delivery for technical staff. They will reinforce the technical standards and quality expectations set by the Director of Technical Services and Principals. 

People Leadership & Supervision 

Serve as the primary supervisor for technical staff at the Project Manager tier, with roughly 5–8 direct reports and 25–30 staff in total scope, owning staffing decisions, workload balance, and day-to-day personnel matters, including scheduling and time-off requests 
Hold regular one-on-ones and be a reliable, present first point of contact for the team’s questions, concerns, and growth 
Support staff through challenges on-site and with clients, project personnel, and peers, advocating for staff while balancing business and team needs 
Reinforce the technical standards, quality expectations, and compliance practices set by the Director and Principals consistently and fairly across the team 

Organizational Leadership 

Serve as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, translating business strategy into clear direction for the team 
Partner with Operations, Finance, and HR to support staff and team needs 
Contribute ideas to continuously improve culture so staff feel safe, heard, and supported 
Own retention commitments and day-to-day execution of the career architecture for the team 
Help build the team structure as Sequoia grows 

Performance & Career Development 

Run performance management that people trust through Sequoia’s quarterly review process: on schedule, with meaningful goals, honest coaching, and recognition that encourage career growth at Sequoia 
Make advancement real by ensuring staff get the assignments, training, credentials, and mentorship their next roles require, measured against Sequoia’s published promotion criteria 
Strengthen the Project Manager pipeline through leadership training and guidance 

Talent Strategy 

Identify hiring needs with Principal team proactively, anticipating growth, workload, and attrition before they become gaps, and own recruiting, interviewing, and hiring for the team 
Coordinate onboarding and training strategy of new technical staff with Principals and Human Resources 
Plan staffing to meet project demand and business development growth, including project-based hires and adjustments to team size 

Staffing & Project Support 

Balance assignments so utilization targets are met and field and office schedules fit each person’s role and level 
Improve how projects are run and staffed 
Identify and resolve project-level staffing, delivery, and technical issues, drawing on the right internal expertise, and escalate division-level and client-facing decisions to the Director 

Desired Experience and Competencies 

Sequoia Ecological Consulting seeks a proven people leader from the environmental consulting industry who leads with a collaborative leadership style and is able to translate between business and team needs. We're looking for someone eager to grow with Sequoia and make a real difference: someone energized by shaping a new role, investing in people's careers, and helping build a team that does meaningful work for California's environment. 

The ideal candidate is someone technical staff trust with their workload, their development, and their careers, bringing strong technical grounding alongside leadership, management skill, and consulting fluency. 

People Leadership & Trust Building 

10+ years of environmental consulting experience, including 5+ years directly supervising professional staff: reviews, coaching, corrective action, and career development 
Demonstrated record of building, developing, and retaining professional teams 
Ability to advocate for staff while balancing their needs with the needs of the business 
Fairness and consistency in applying performance and promotion criteria across a team 
Empathy and the ability to build trust across all levels of the team 

Consulting & Technical Acumen  

Substantial environmental consulting experience in California, with a strong understanding of how consulting teams, project delivery, utilization, project margins, and client service operate 
Proven project management experience, including managing clients and subcontractors 
Technical background in a discipline related to Sequoia’s work, such as biology, botany, aquatic ecology, or restoration 
Working knowledge of California’s environmental regulatory landscape, including CEQA, NEPA, ESA, and CESA, sufficient to lead technical professionals credibly 
Resourcefulness; doesn’t need to have every answer, but knows how to find it 

Team & Talent Building  

Experience forecasting staffing needs and shaping team structure around workload, growth, and capacity 
Understanding of what strong technical talent looks like and ability to contribute to hiring decisions 
Ability to identify hiring needs based on workload, growth, and team capacity 

Communication & Composure  

Excellent organizational, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills 
Ability to have direct, fair, and timely conversations, with sound judgment 
Ability to remain calm under pressure and juggle competing priorities without losing focus 
Adaptability in a growing firm with evolving structures and needs 

Preferred Qualifications 

Experience implementing leadership development, training, or mentoring programs 
Technical expertise in biology, botany, aquatic ecology, or restoration 
Designated Biologist status or equivalent agency-recognized qualifications 
Graduate degree, research, or agency experience 
Established regulatory agency relationships 
Experience at an environmental consulting firm of 25 or more people 
Experience with cross-functional collaboration with operations, finance, and HR 
A bachelor’s degree in biology, ecology, environmental science, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and industry experience 

Compensation 

This is a full-time, exempt, benefit-eligible position. The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $140,000–$160,000, commensurate with experience. 

Sequoia offers a comprehensive benefits package, including health, dental, and vision coverage; 401(k) with company match; and a professional development budget. 

Location and Requirements 

This position is remote, based in California, with a preference for Bay Area candidates. The Technical Services Manager will be expected in the Walnut Creek office quarterly for team meetings, key events, and time with staff; quarterly travel costs will be covered by Sequoia. The role also requires occasional travel to Sequoia’s other Northern and Southern California offices, project sites, and field locations. Some weekend or after-hours availability is needed to support field schedules and team needs. 

To Apply 

Please visit https://sequoiaeco.com/careers to apply. 

Before taking the time to apply, please confirm your answer to each of the following must-have, non-negotiable requirements is yes: 

10+ years of environmental consulting experience, including work in California 
Experience directly supervising professional staff 
Experience managing projects, clients, or subcontractors 
Familiarity with California’s environmental regulatory landscape (such as CEQA, NEPA, ESA, and CESA) 
Ability to be in office quarterly for team and project needs  

Instead of a cover letter, please submit your resume and written answers to the four questions below (up to 200 words each). If possible, combine both into a single document saved as “LastName_TSM.” 

Mission Alignment: Why are you excited about this role, and why now in your career? What draws you to our work and to Sequoia? 
Team Leadership: Describe your experience building or leading a team in consulting. What do you put in place to develop and retain the people on it? 
Coaching & Mentorship: Describe your approach to ongoing performance management and professional development. How do you keep people growing over time, and how do you approach coaching conversations when someone needs to course-correct? 
Consulting & Technical Fluency: Describe your experience leading technical staff while balancing the needs of your team, clients, and firm leadership. How do you build credibility with technical experts and stay steady under pressure? 

Interested candidates should apply by November 15, 2026, for priority consideration. You can expect to hear back from us about the status of your application by the end of November. Applications received after that date will be accepted and considered alongside the existing candidate pool until the position is filled. 
Contact
Helai Karimi
[email removed] (preferred contact method)

Position Title: AmeriCorps Individual Placement – Engineering Technician 
Conservation Legacy Program: Southeast Conservation Corps    
Site Location: Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest, Blue Ridge Ranger District 
Address:  
2042 Highway 515 W 
Blairsville, GA 30512 
Term of Service: 50 weeks 
Start Date: 04/05/2027 
End Date: 03/17/2028 
AmeriCorps Slot Classification: 1700 hr   
Status: This is a full-time, seasonal, 50-week, 1700-hour AmeriCorps National Service Program.  
Benefits:  
Segal AmeriCorps Education Award of $7,395.00 upon successful completion of the program 
Living allowance of $480.00 per week, paid bi-weekly 
Additional Benefit of $465.00 per week, paid bi-weekly 
Other Benefits: AmeriCorps health insurance, uniform shirts, personal protective equipment, Public Land Corps Hiring Authority Certificate (upon successful completion of hours), member assistance program, and other professional development opportunities available.  
Positions Available: 1 
 Purpose 
Southeast Conservation Corps (SECC):    
Empowering youth and adults to cultivate compassion, responsibility and life skills through community service, hard work and land stewardship.  
 Southeast Conservation Corps, a program of Conservation Legacy, is a non-profit AmeriCorps program. We engage youth (age 15-17) and young adults (ages 18-30, up to 35 for veterans) in service projects on public lands throughout the Southeast. SECC collaborates with land management agencies (United States Forest Service, National Park Service, State Parks, local municipalities, and non-profits) to host day or overnight camping crews and individual placements.  
 Our AmeriCorps positions provide impactful educational and service opportunities that benefit both communities and landscapes. SECC’s participants reflect the population of the Southeast region, including youth, graduates, veterans, and individuals from various backgrounds.  
 United States Forest Service: 
The phrase “Caring for the Land and Serving People,” captures the Forest Service mission. As set forth in law, the mission is to achieve quality land management under the sustainable multiple-use management concept to meet the many needs of people.  
 Blue Ridge Ranger District: 
The Blue Ridge Ranger District Civil Engineering Program is responsible for approximately 500 miles of Forest Service roads within the district's area of responsibility. Duties include data collection, survey, maintenance, repair, and inspection of roadways ranging from suitable passenger cars to high clearance vehicle-only roads. Additionally, Civil Engineering duties include data collection, inspection, survey, and limited scope maintenance and repair of Forest Service facilities. 
 Position Overview:  
This Individual Placement is designed to provide an entry-level professional opportunity to serve directly with a federal land management agency, developing relevant skills, qualifications, and experience. The projects will focus on field data collection to provide a comprehensive assessment of current conditions in relation to recent natural disasters and weather impacts. Hurricane Helene, along with many other recent impacts, has created significant impacts on the Blue Ridge Ranger District.  
 The Individual Placement will serve alongside Forest Service technicians and specialists in various resource areas, including trail management, wilderness stewardship, engineering, archaeology, outdoor recreational facilities, wildlife management, silviculture, forestry, and wildland fire management. Most tasks will be primarily focused on erosion control. Storm-damaged or improperly maintained roads lead to erosion, resulting in excessive entry of pollutants into waterways. Out of the district’s 500 miles of road, it is estimated to seek improvements of approximately 150 to 200 miles during this period of disaster repair.  
 While the service project will focus on road engineering related tasks, utilizing GIS technology and associated devices to collect real-time data from the field, the exposure and training are designed to provide the Individual Placement with the experience necessary to compete for an entry-level position with a land management agency upon program completion.  
 Description of Duties: 
Roadway Disaster Data Collection  
Serve with the Supervisor to gain an understanding of the data needed and the overall intent of the assessment.  
Build an assessment plan for the district to prioritize different resource needs and concerns.  
Gain proficiency with GIS technology and applications   
Keep consistent records of data gathered.  
 Maintenance Planning  
Serve with the Engineering Technician to gain an understanding of road condition expectations.    
Assist Engineering with routine activities to include road condition surveys, site assessments, mapping, road feature counts, etc...   
Assist in Engineering to prioritize needs.    
Assist Engineering in plan development, 811 marking, cost estimate, and procurement.   
 Maintenance Operations 
Assist Engineering with safety notifications, site preparation, and pre-stage.  
Assist Engineering with mobilization.  
Use a variety of hand tools, power tools, and limited complexity equipment operation under the supervision of certified personnel.   
Assist team with clean-up and monitoring after the day is completed.  
 Potential environmental/human risk involved with this term of service: uneven terrain, physical exertion, inclement weather, and remote service sites.   
 Qualifications: 
United States citizen, United States national, or a lawful permanent resident alien  
Must be between the ages of 18 and 30, or up to 35 if a military veteran.    
Has received a high school diploma or equivalency certificate; or has not dropped out of elementary or secondary school to enroll as an AmeriCorps participant, and agrees to obtain a high school diploma or its equivalent before using the education award  
Agrees to provide information to establish eligibility and to complete a National Service Criminal History Check  
Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.  
Strong interest in road construction, serving outdoors, and natural resource management.  
Proven ability to complete assignments and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.   
Comfortable navigating by map throughout the forest, including areas with limited or no cell coverage.  
You must possess a valid driver’s license and pass Conservation Legacy’s Driver Insurability requirements.  
  Preferred Qualifications: 
Experience with hand tools, power tools, and tractors.   
Crosscut or chainsaw sawyer Certification.   
Experience with navigation by map and terrain association.  
Experience with ESRI Field Maps, Survey123, and ArcGIS software.  
 Transportation:   
A personal vehicle is required to report to/from the service site/office, and for all personal business. A USFS/SECC vehicle will be provided for transportation to conduct operations within the forest. This Individual Placement must be a driver and pass Conservation Legacy’s driver insurability requirements. 
 Housing: 
Housing will not be provided. USFS staff will assist with finding housing in the local area near the park.  
 Physical Requirements: 
Conservation Legacy is committed to the full consideration of all qualified individuals and will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to perform essential functions. Some positions may require periodic overnight travel, non-traditional hours, ability to move across varied terrain, use program-specific tools and a range of technology on an infrequent or frequent basis. Exerting up to 25 pounds of force occasionally to lift, carry, push, pull, or otherwise move objects. Ability to safely drive an organizational vehicle may also be required for some positions. If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during application or recruiting process, please send a request to the hiring manager.   
  Time Requirements: 
Typically, this position is expected to serve from 8 am – 5pm, Monday through Friday, 40 hours per week – but exact service schedules may vary and will include evening and weekend service depending on project needs.  
A half hour lunch break will not be counted towards AmeriCorps service.  
Members may be required to participate in national, state, or local service projects or events as part of their service term.   
 Orientation and Training: 
Members will receive an orientation that includes training on AmeriCorps prohibited and unallowable activities.    
Defensive Driving – how to drive on gravel/USFS roads 
ArcGIS, Survey123, FieldMaps, Avenza, USDA Guidelines for Maintenance Levels 
 Evaluation and Reporting: 
As an AmeriCorps member, performance will be evaluated on whether the member has completed the required number of hours, the member has satisfactorily completed assignments, and if the member has met other performance criteria that were clearly communicated at the beginning of the term of service.   
Reporting requirements include, but are not limited to:   
Bi-weekly timesheets  
Monthly Accomplishment Report  
Narrative Monthly Report.  
Bi-Monthly Check-Ins  
Midterm and Final Evals  
Exiting Tasks  
 Substance Free: 
In accordance with a drug-free environment, alcohol and drugs are prohibited while participating in AmeriCorps and program activities and while on organization property.    
 If you have questions about the position, please contact:   
Jonathan Key 
Civil Engineering Program Manager 
USFS: Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest 
Blue Ridge Ranger District 
[email removed]  
 If you have questions about the application process, please contact:   
Angela Gerstner 
Individual Placements Coordinator 
Southeast Conservation Corps   
[email removed]  
 Conservation Legacy is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.   
 We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you need assistance and/or reasonable accommodations due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please send a request to the hiring manager.

Angela Gerstner
